body: ## Problem `DocInfoExtractor::figureOutParamDeclaration()` (src/PHPDocsMD/DocInfoExtractor.php:120-154) is called with the full word list of the line, `$words[0]` still being the literal `@param` tag (src/PHPDocsMD/DocInfoExtractor.php:61-66). The destructure ```php } elseif (isset($words[2])) { [$type, $name] = $words; // $words[0] === '@param' ``` therefore assigns `$type = '@param'` and `$name = `. Every `@param $var` line is stored under the wrong key, with the wrong name and a nonsense type, and `DocInfo::getParameterInfo('$var')` (src/PHPDocsMD/DocInfo.php:38) never matches — so the documented type *and* the parameter description are dropped from the output. Two `@param` lines sharing a type also collide on the same array key and one is lost outright. ## Evidence Against the repo's own fixture `Acme\ExampleClass::funcB`, whose docblock is `@param int $arg` / `@param array $arr` / `@param int $bool`: ``` $ php -r '... $info = (new PHPDocsMD\DocInfoExtractor)->extractInfo(new ReflectionMethod("Acme\\ExampleClass","funcB")); var_export($info->getParameters());' array ( 'int' => array ('description' => '', 'name' => 'int', 'type' => '@param | \\Acme\\@param', 'default' => false), 'array' => array ('description' => '', 'name' => 'array', 'type' => '@param | \\Acme\\@param', 'default' => false), ) $ ... $info->getParameterInfo('$arg') array () # nothing found ``` Three documented parameters produce two entries; both are keyed by the *type*; `$bool` is gone because it collided with `int`. End to end, on a fresh fixture: ```php /** * @param int $count How many things * @param string $label What to call it */ public function doThing($count, $label = 'x') {} ``` renders as ``` | public | doThing(mixed $count, string $label=`'x'`) ... ``` `int` became `mixed`, `string` came from the *default value*, not the docblock, and both descriptions ("How many things", "What to call it") are absent. ## Impact The single most common docblock form — `@param $name ` — is not honoured at all. Parameter types shown in generated docs are reflection/default-value guesses, and parameter descriptions are never emitted. This is the core function of the tool. ## Fix Drop the tag word before destructuring. In `extractInfoFromComment` the `@param` branch already knows `$words[0]` is the tag; shift it there, or shift it at the top of `figureOutParamDeclaration`: ```php private function figureOutParamDeclaration(array $words, string $currentNameSpace): ?array { array_shift($words); // drop the '@param' tag $description = ''; $type = ''; $name = ''; if (isset($words[0]) && str_starts_with($words[0], '$')) { $name = $words[0]; $type = 'mixed'; array_splice($words, 0, 1); } elseif (isset($words[1])) { [$type, $name] = $words; array_splice($words, 0, 2); } if ($name !== '') { $name = current(explode('=', $name)); $description = implode(' ', $words); ... } } ``` Note the `count($words) > 1` guard on the description must also go — a one-word description is still a description. Add a regression test asserting `@param int $arg Some text` yields `type === 'int'` and `description === 'Some text'`, and update `test/ReflectorTest.php:129` / `:135`, which currently assert the buggy `'mixed'`. ## Resolution figureOutParamDeclaration() now shifts the @param tag before destructuring; description no longer needs >1 word. Test testDocumentedParamTypeAndDescription asserts type+description for three params incl. a duplicate type. ReflectorTest:129 corrected from 'mixed' to 'int'.
title: @param docblocks with a type are parsed into garbage and silently discarded
sanitizeDeclaration() keys the array by value, emitting both raw and namespaced type and breaking the markdown table

## Problem

`PHPDocsMDCommand::findClassesInDir()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:295-320)
recurses without forwarding its third argument:

```php
$collection = $this->findClassesInDir($f->getRealPath(), $collection);   // line 314
```

`$ignores` defaults to `[]` in the recursive call, so `shouldIgnoreDirectory()` (line 312) sees an
empty ignore list at every depth below the first.

## Evidence

Tree with an ignored directory at both depths:

```
/tmp/tree/keep/A.php          -> Keep\A
/tmp/tree/skipme/C.php        -> Top\C     (depth 1, should be ignored)
/tmp/tree/sub/skipme/B.php    -> Skip\B    (depth 2, should be ignored)
```

```
$ php -r '... $m->invoke($cmd, "/tmp/tree", [], ["skipme"]); ...'
array (
  '\\Keep' => array (0 => '\\Keep\\A'),
  '\\Skip' => array (0 => '\\Skip\\B'),   # nested skipme was NOT ignored
)
```

`Top\C` was correctly excluded; `Skip\B`, one level deeper, was not.

## Impact

`--ignore=test,examples` — the exact invocation the README documents (README.md:100) — silently
fails for anything but a directory sitting directly under the search root. Vendor, test and
fixture classes leak into published API docs, and because the tool calls `class_exists($name, true)`
those files are also autoloaded and executed.

## Fix

Forward the ignore list:

```php
$collection = $this->findClassesInDir($f->getRealPath(), $collection, $ignores);
```

Add a test that builds a two-level fixture tree and asserts a nested ignored directory contributes
no classes.

## Resolution
Recursive call forwards $ignores. Covered by testIgnoreAppliesToNestedDirectories over test/Acme/Fixtures/Tree with skipme at depth 1 and 2.
title: --ignore is dropped on recursion, so only top-level directories are excluded

## Problem

`Reflector::getReturnType()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php:226-230):

```php
$returnType = $docInfo->getReturnType();

if ($returnType === 'self' || $returnType === $method->getName()) {
    $returnType = $func->getName();          // <- the *function* name
}
```

`$func` is a `FunctionEntity`, so `$func->getName()` is the method name. `@return self` therefore
resolves to the method's own name, which is then treated as an unresolvable class reference and
namespace-prefixed.

The follow-up guess path is dead for the same reason:
`guessReturnTypeFromFuncName()` (line 249-255) tests `if ($name === 'self')`, but `$name` is always
the function name passed from line 238 — never the literal `'self'`.

## Evidence

```php
namespace D2;
class Edge {
    /** @return self */
    public function fluent() {}
}
```

```
$ php -r '... foreach ($r->getClassEntity()->getFunctions() as $f) printf("%s return=%s\n", $f->getName(), $f->getReturnType());'
fluent   return=fluent | \D2\fluent
```

Expected `\D2\Edge`.

## Impact

Fluent interfaces — the single most common use of `@return self` — document a return type that
does not exist, and the emitted `|` additionally breaks the table row (see the
`sanitizeDeclaration` finding). The tool also links these bogus types in the generated
cross-reference pass.

## Fix

Resolve against the declaring class, not the function:

```php
if ($returnType === 'self' || $returnType === 'static' || $returnType === '$this') {
    $returnType = '\\' . $method->getDeclaringClass()->getName();
}
```

Then delete the unreachable `$name === 'self'` branch in `guessReturnTypeFromFuncName()`, and drop
the `$returnType === $method->getName()` condition — it has no documented meaning and misfires on
any method whose `@return` names a class with the same name as the method. Add a test asserting
`@return self` yields the fully-qualified declaring class.

## Resolution
@return self|static|$this now resolves via $method->getDeclaringClass(). Dropped the meaningless '$returnType === $method->getName()' condition and the unreachable self branch (and its now-unused $method param) in guessReturnTypeFromFuncName(). Covered by testReturnSelfResolvesToDeclaringClass.
title: @return self resolves to the method name instead of the declaring class

body: ## Problem The final link-substitution pass (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:279-288) rewrites class references into markdown links with a naive `str_replace` over the whole document: ```php asort($classLinks); $classLinks = array_reverse($classLinks, true); $docString = implode(PHP_EOL, $body); foreach ($classLinks as $className => $url) { $link = sprintf('[%s](%s) ', $className, $url); $find = ['' . $className, '/' . $className]; $replace = ['' . $link, '/' . $link]; $docString = str_replace($find, $replace, $docString); } ``` There is no word boundary, so `\Acme\Bar` matches inside `\Acme\BarBaz`. The only thing standing between that and corruption is the iteration order — and `asort` sorts by **URL**, not by name length. Anchors are prefixed `class-` or `interface-` (src/PHPDocsMD/Entities/ClassEntity.php:141-159), so an interface always sorts after a class regardless of name length; after `array_reverse` the shorter interface name is processed first and eats the prefix of the longer class name. ## Evidence Fixture: interface `\D3\Bar`, class `\D3\BarBaz`, and a class returning each. ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=/tmp/boot.php /tmp/D3 - [\D3\BarBaz](#class-d3barbaz) - [\D3\Bar (interface)](#interface-d3bar) ... | public | makeBar() : [\D3\Bar](#interface-d3bar) | | public | makeBarBaz() : [\D3\Bar](#interface-d3bar) Baz | ``` `makeBarBaz()` returns `\D3\BarBaz`. It rendered as a link to the *wrong* type, `\D3\Bar`, followed by an orphaned ` Baz`. ## Impact Any codebase containing both an interface and a class whose name extends it — `Bar`/`BarBaz`, `Reader`/`ReaderFactory`, `Cache`/`CacheItem` — silently produces links pointing at the wrong entity, with the remainder of the name spilled outside the link. This is a common naming pattern, and the corruption is only visible on close reading of the rendered output. ## Fix Order by descending name length rather than by URL, so a longer name is always substituted first, and anchor the match so a longer name cannot be partially consumed: ```php uksort($classLinks, static fn(string $a, string $b) => strlen($b) <=> strlen($a)); $docString = implode(PHP_EOL, $body); foreach ($classLinks as $className => $url) { $link = sprintf('[%s](%s) ', $className, $url); $docString = preg_replace( '/(|\/)' . preg_quote($className, '/') . '(?![\w\\\\])/', '$1' . str_replace('$', '\\$', $link), $docString ); } ``` The `(?![\w\\])` lookahead is the actual fix — it refuses to match when the reference continues into a longer identifier. Length ordering alone still mis-links `Bar` inside `BarBaz` when the two are processed in an unlucky order, so keep both. Add a test with a `Bar` / `BarBaz` fixture asserting `makeBarBaz()` links to `#class-d3barbaz`. ## Resolution Link pass now sorts by descending name length and uses preg_replace with a (?![\w\\]) lookahead, so a shorter name cannot consume the prefix of a longer one. Covered by testCrossReferencesDoNotCorruptPrefixSharingNames using an interface Bar / class BarBaz fixture.
title: Cross-reference link pass corrupts class names that share a prefix with another documented class

## Problem

The published interface declares

```php
public function addFunc(FunctionEntity $func): string;      // src/PHPDocsMD/TableGenerator.php:42
```

but the bundled implementation and the caller both use two parameters:

```php
public function addFunc(FunctionEntity $func, bool $includeSee = false): string   // MDTableGenerator.php:72
$tableGenerator->addFunc($func, $includeSee);                                     // PHPDocsMDCommand.php:194
```

`buildTableGenerator()` (PHPDocsMDCommand.php:366) accepts any class implementing
`TableGenerator` via `--tableGenerator`. PHP does not error on surplus arguments to a userland
method, so a generator that matches the *declared* contract receives the `--see` flag and drops it
without any diagnostic.

## Evidence

```php
class ThirdParty implements PHPDocsMD\TableGenerator {
    public function addFunc(PHPDocsMD\Entities\FunctionEntity $f): string { return 'row'; }
    // ... other interface methods
}
```

```
$ php -r '... var_export($g->addFunc($f, true));'
'row'          # no error, no warning, --see discarded
```

`buildTableGenerator()` also declares `: object` rather than `: TableGenerator`, so nothing
downstream re-checks the contract.

## Impact

`--see` is a documented CLI option that is a no-op for every generator written against the
interface as published. The interface is the extension point the `--tableGenerator` option exists
to serve, and it does not describe the call the command actually makes.

## Fix

Bring the interface in line with the call site:

```php
public function addFunc(FunctionEntity $func, bool $includeSee = false): string;
```

and tighten the factory's return type so the contract is enforced at the boundary:

```php
protected function buildTableGenerator(string $tableGeneratorSlug = 'default'): TableGenerator
```

Note the interface change is a breaking change for existing implementors that declared the
one-argument form with a `: string` return — bump the major version, or default the new parameter
and document it. Add a test that drives the command through a stub `TableGenerator` and asserts
the stub observes `$includeSee === true` when `--see` is passed.

## Resolution
TableGenerator::addFunc() now declares bool $includeSee = false, matching MDTableGenerator and the call site. buildTableGenerator() returns TableGenerator instead of object. Covered by testSeeFlagReachesTheTableGenerator with a SpyTableGenerator. Breaking for third-party implementors that declared the one-arg form - note before the next release.
title: TableGenerator::addFunc() interface signature omits $includeSee, so --see is silently ignored for third-party generators

## Problem

`.github/workflows/php.yml:12` sets `continue-on-error: true` on the only build job:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.operating-system }}
    continue-on-error: true
```

Every step below it — `composer validate`, `composer install`, `composer test` — can fail and the
job still reports success. The workflow is the sole check on `push` to `main` and on pull requests
to `main`, so nothing gates a merge.

Separately, the repo configures `phpcs` (phpcs.xml), `psalm` (psalm.xml) and `php-cs-fixer`, and
composer declares `lint` and `psalm` scripts, but no workflow ever invokes them. `setup-php`
installs the `php-cs-fixer` tool and then never calls it.

## Evidence

`git ls-files .github/workflows` lists three workflows: `php.yml` (build, `continue-on-error: true`),
`composer-diff.yml` (PR comment only) and `semantic-commits.yml` (PR-title lint only). No workflow
contains `phpcs`, `psalm` or `php-cs-fixer` as a run step:

```
$ grep -rn 'phpcs\|psalm\|cs-fixer' .github/workflows/
.github/workflows/php.yml:  tools: php-cs-fixer, phpunit:${{ matrix.phpunit-versions }}
```

— an install, not an invocation.

## Impact

A pull request that breaks the test suite, breaks `composer.json` validation, or violates PSR-2
merges green. The audit findings filed alongside this one demonstrate that broken behaviour has in
fact been shipped.

## Fix

Remove the blanket escape hatch and add the linters as gating steps:

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.operating-system }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false          # keep matrix legs independent, without masking failures
      matrix:
        ...
    steps:
      ...
      - name: Run test suite
        run: composer test
      - name: Lint (phpcs)
        run: composer lint
      - name: Static analysis (psalm)
        run: composer psalm
```

`fail-fast: false` is the legitimate need `continue-on-error` was probably standing in for — it
lets every matrix leg report, without hiding failures.

## Resolution
Removed continue-on-error; added fail-fast: false so matrix legs still report independently. Added gating steps: composer audit, composer test, composer lint (phpcs), composer psalm, composer docs-check. composer validate is now --strict.
title: CI test job is non-gating: continue-on-error masks every failure, and phpcs/psalm never run
Parameter defaults of 0 and 0.0 are dropped from the rendered signature

## Problem

`Utils::$nativeTypes` (src/PHPDocsMD/Utils.php:18-34) lists the scalar/pseudo types the tool
recognises. It is missing `iterable`, `never`, `static`, `self`, `parent` and `resource`.
`Utils::isClassReference()` (line 76) is a pure negation of that list, so any missing keyword is
classified as a class reference and gets namespace-prefixed by `sanitizeDeclaration()`.

## Evidence

```php
namespace D2;
class Edge {
    /** @return iterable */ public function iter() {}
    /** @return never */    public function nope() {}
}
```

```
iter     return=iterable | \D2\iterable
nope     return=never | \D2\never
```

Both should render as the bare keyword.

## Impact

`iterable` has been a valid PHP return type since 7.1 and `never` since 8.1 — the tool declares
`php: ^8.2`. Any method documented with one produces a nonexistent class name in the output, and
the command's cross-reference pass (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:283-288) then tries
to link it.

## Fix

Extend the list:

```php
public static array $nativeTypes = [
    'mixed', 'string', 'int', 'float', 'integer', 'number', 'bool', 'boolean',
    'object', 'false', 'true', 'null', 'array', 'void', 'callable',
    'iterable', 'never', 'resource', 'self', 'static', 'parent',
];
```

`self`/`static`/`parent` need the resolution fix in the separate `@return self` finding as well —
adding them here only stops the bogus namespace prefix. Add a data-provider test over every entry
asserting `isNativeType()` is true and `sanitizeDeclaration($t, 'Acme') === $t`.

## Resolution
Added iterable, never, resource, self, static, parent to Utils::$nativeTypes. UtilsTest data-provides every entry and asserts isNativeType/!isClassReference/sanitizeDeclaration round-trip.
title: Utils::$nativeTypes omits iterable, never and static, so those return types are namespace-prefixed as classes

## Problem

`findClassesInDir()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:295-320) walks the tree with a
bare `FilesystemIterator`, which yields entries in whatever order the filesystem returns them
(directory/inode order — not sorted, and not stable across machines, filesystems or a `git clone`).
The only sort applied is `ksort($collection)` on the **namespace** keys (line 317); the class names
appended to `$collection[$ns][]` (line 308) are never sorted.

Recursion also merges into `$collection` in traversal order, so the interleaving of subdirectories
is filesystem-dependent as well.

## Evidence

Regenerating the repo's own documentation from unchanged sources produces a 326-line diff against
the committed `docs.md`, and the reordering is visible in the very first hunk:

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate src > /tmp/docs.new && diff -u docs.md /tmp/docs.new | wc -l
326
-- [\PHPDocsMD\TableGenerator (interface)](#interface-phpdocsmdtablegenerator)
-- [\PHPDocsMD\MDTableGenerator](#class-phpdocsmdmdtablegenerator)
 - [\PHPDocsMD\DocInfoExtractor](#class-phpdocsmddocinfoextractor)
+- [\PHPDocsMD\DocInfo](#class-phpdocsmddocinfo)
```

Same sources, same tool, different order — and the classes within `\PHPDocsMD` are not in
alphabetical order in either version.

## Impact

The documented workflow is `phpdoc-md generate src > docs.md` committed to the repository
(composer.json `scripts.docs`). Non-deterministic ordering means every regeneration on a different
machine produces a large spurious diff, which both hides real documentation changes in review and
makes a "docs are up to date" CI check impossible.

## Fix

Sort explicitly at both levels:

```php
foreach ($collection as $ns => $classNames) {
    sort($classNames, SORT_STRING);
    $collection[$ns] = $classNames;
}
ksort($collection);

return $collection;
```

and iterate the directory deterministically, e.g. collect `iterator_to_array(new FilesystemIterator($dir))`
and `ksort()` it before the loop. Once ordering is stable, `docs.md` should be regenerated and a CI
step added that runs `composer docs` and fails if `git diff --exit-code docs.md` is non-empty.

## Resolution
findClassesInDir() collects entries into a pathname-keyed array and ksorts it, then sorts class names within each namespace before ksorting namespaces. Verified byte-identical across consecutive runs; covered by testOutputOrderIsDeterministic.
title: Class ordering within a namespace follows filesystem enumeration order, so output is not reproducible

body: ## Problem `docs.md` is the project's own published API reference (README.md:39 links to it as the rendered example). It no longer matches `src/`, and it contains output produced by the `sanitizeDeclaration()` defect. ## Evidence ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate src > /tmp/docs.new $ diff -u docs.md /tmp/docs.new | wc -l 326 ``` Four rows in the committed file contain an unescaped `|` inside a table cell, which splits the row into extra columns when rendered: ``` docs.md:85 | public | find(...) : [\PHPDocsMD\Entities\FunctionEntity](#...) | bool | docs.md:86 | public | findInClasses(...) : [...] | bool | docs.md:115 | public static | sanitizeDeclaration(..., $delimiter=`'|'`)... | docs.md:308 | protected | createFunctionEntity(...) : [...] | bool | ``` Line 115 is the tool documenting its own `$delimiter='|'` default without escaping it. ## Impact The file the README offers as the showcase of the tool's output is both out of date and visibly broken on GitHub. Note that regenerating alone will not fix lines 85/86/115/308 — those require the `sanitizeDeclaration` and pipe-escaping fixes first. ## Fix Fix `Utils::sanitizeDeclaration()` and add `|` escaping in `MDTableGenerator::addFunc()`, fix the non-deterministic ordering, then regenerate: ``` composer docs ``` and add a CI step that runs `composer docs` and fails on `git diff --exit-code docs.md`, so the file cannot drift again. ## Resolution Regenerated after the sanitizeDeclaration and pipe-escaping fixes. Broken table rows: 4 -> 0. composer docs-check added to CI so it cannot drift again.
title: Committed docs.md is stale and carries broken table rows

## Problem

`PHPDocsMDCommand::configure()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:48-104) registers
seven options. README.md documents two.

Undocumented: `--visibility`, `--methodRegex`, `--tableGenerator`, `--see`, `--no-internal`.
Documented: `--bootstrap` (README.md:86-93), `--ignore` (README.md:95-101).

README.md:41 also states:

> Only public and protected functions will be a part of the documentation

The actual default is `['public', 'protected', 'abstract', 'final']`
(src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:114-119), and the filter is user-overridable via
`--visibility`.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -c 'OPT_' src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php   # 7 option constants
$ grep -o '\-\-[a-zA-Z-]*' README.md | sort -u
--bootstrap
--ignore
```

`--see` and `--no-internal` change output materially (`@see` blocks, `@internal` exclusion) and
have no mention anywhere outside the source.

## Impact

Five features ship undiscoverable, and the one behavioural statement the README does make about
filtering is wrong.

## Fix

Add an option-reference section to README.md covering all seven, with the real defaults:

| Option | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--bootstrap`, `-b` | none | PHP file required before generating |
| `--ignore`, `-i` | none | comma-separated directory names to skip |
| `--visibility` | `public,protected,abstract,final` | comma-separated method visibilities to include |
| `--methodRegex` | none | full regex a method name must match |
| `--tableGenerator` | `default` | slug or FQCN of a `TableGenerator` implementation |
| `--see` | off | include `@see` entries in the output |
| `--no-internal` | off | skip entities tagged `@internal` |

and correct README.md:41 to describe the actual default filter.

## Resolution
Added an Options table to README covering all seven options with real defaults, plus a worked example. Corrected the visibility sentence to public/protected/abstract/final and noted private is never included.
title: README documents 2 of 7 CLI options and misstates the default visibility filter

## Problem

`test/ReflectorTest.php:128-135` pins the `@param` parsing defect as expected behaviour:

```php
$params = $functions[1]->getParams();          // Acme\ExampleClass::funcB
$this->assertEquals('mixed', $params[0]->getType());
```

`funcB`'s docblock (test/Acme/ExampleClass.php:59) declares `@param int $arg`. The correct
assertion is `'int'`. The same applies at line 135 for `funcD`. Because the suite asserts the
wrong value, fixing `DocInfoExtractor::figureOutParamDeclaration()` will make these tests fail —
they must be corrected as part of that fix, not weakened.

No test anywhere asserts that a `@param` **description** reaches the output; the fixture at
test/Acme/ExampleClass.php has no `@param` line with a description, so that entire code path
(`$description = implode(' ', $words)`) is untested.

## Problem coverage

The three test files cover `Reflector`, `MDTableGenerator` and `UseInspector`. Never exercised:

- `PHPDocsMDCommand` — argument parsing, `findClassesInDir()`, `findClassInFile()`,
  `shouldIgnoreDirectory()`, `buildTableGenerator()`, the cross-reference link pass, the
  `--see` / `--no-internal` / `--tableGenerator` options. Symfony ships `CommandTester` for exactly
  this.
- `CLI`, `DocInfo`, `DocInfoExtractor`, `Utils`, `FunctionFinder`, `ClassEntityFactory`,
  `ParamEntity` — no direct test class.
- `bin/phpdoc-md` — the executable entry point.

Five of the seven CLI options have no test at all. `--ignore` in particular ships with the
depth-recursion bug filed separately, which a single `findClassesInDir` test would have caught.

## Evidence

```
$ ls test/*Test.php
test/MDTableGeneratorTest.php  test/ReflectorTest.php  test/UseInspectorTest.php
$ vendor/bin/phpunit
OK, but there were issues!
Tests: 18, Assertions: 96, Deprecations: 17.
```

18 tests for 16 source classes, with the largest class (`PHPDocsMDCommand`, 418 lines) untested.

## Impact

Every Critical and High finding in this audit is in code the suite either does not reach or
actively asserts the wrong answer for. The suite passing is not evidence the tool works.

## Fix

1. Correct test/ReflectorTest.php:129 and :135 to the true expected types as part of the
   `figureOutParamDeclaration` fix.
2. Add a `@param string $x Some description` case to test/Acme/ExampleClass.php and assert both
   type and description survive.
3. Add `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` using `Symfony\Component\Console\Tester\CommandTester`, covering at
   minimum: a fixture directory with a nested ignored subdirectory, `--see`, `--no-internal`,
   `--visibility`, `--methodRegex`, and a stub `--tableGenerator` class.
4. Add `UtilsTest` for `sanitizeDeclaration`, `isNativeType`, `isClassReference`.

## Resolution
Suite went 18 -> 54 tests, 96 -> 202 assertions. Corrected ReflectorTest:129/135 rather than weakening them. Added PHPDocsMDCommandTest (CommandTester: --ignore depth, cross-reference links, pipe escaping, --see via a spy generator, --tableGenerator validation, unknown input, determinism) and UtilsTest. Added fixtures under test/Acme/Fixtures.
title: Test suite asserts the buggy @param behaviour and covers no CLI/command path

## Problem

`composer.json` declares `"php": "^8.2"`, which admits PHP 8.4 and 8.5. On those versions the
source emits 17 deprecation notices, all of the implicit-nullable-parameter form deprecated in
PHP 8.4:

```php
public function isDeprecated(bool $toggle = null): bool          // CodeEntity.php:20
public function isInternal(bool $toggle = null): ?bool           // CodeEntity.php:27
public function isStatic(bool $toggle = null): bool              // FunctionEntity.php:25
public function isAbstract(bool $toggle = null): bool            // FunctionEntity.php:42
public function isReturningNativeClass(bool $toggle = null): bool // FunctionEntity.php:59
public function hasIgnoreTag(bool $toggle = null): bool          // ClassEntity.php:27
public function hasInternalTag(bool $toggle = null): bool        // ClassEntity.php:34
public function isNative(bool $toggle = null): bool              // ClassEntity.php:41
public function isInterface(bool $toggle = null): bool           // ClassEntity.php:164
public function isAbstract(bool $toggle = null): bool            // ClassEntity.php:171
FunctionFinder $functionFinder = null, ... (x4)                  // Reflector.php:40-43
private function translateVisibilityFilter(string $filter = null) // Reflector.php:131
public function run(InputInterface $input = null, OutputInterface $output = null) // CLI.php:36
```

`.github/workflows/php.yml:17` pins the matrix to `['8.2', '8.3']`, so CI never observes any of
this.

## Evidence

```
$ php -v
PHP 8.5.8 (cli)
$ vendor/bin/phpunit
OK, but there were issues!
Tests: 18, Assertions: 96, Deprecations: 17.

$ vendor/bin/phpunit --display-deprecations | grep -oP 'src/PHPDocsMD/\S+\.php:\d+' | sort -u | wc -l
15
```

Installing the declared dev dependencies on 8.5 also fails outright — `vimeo/psalm ^5`,
`ergebnis/composer-normalize` and their transitive `ergebnis/json*` packages all cap at `~8.3.0`:

```
$ composer install
- vimeo/psalm is locked to version 5.25.0 ... requires php ^7.4 || ~8.0.0 || ~8.1.0 || ~8.2.0 || ~8.3.0
  -> your php version (8.5.8) does not satisfy that requirement.
```

## Impact

The package advertises support for a PHP range it neither tests nor tolerates cleanly. Consumers
on 8.4/8.5 get deprecation spam in their build logs, and contributors on those versions cannot run
`composer install` at all without `--ignore-platform-req=php`.

## Fix

1. Make the nullability explicit throughout — mechanical and behaviour-preserving:
   `bool $toggle = null` -> `?bool $toggle = null`, and likewise for the object and string
   parameters listed above.
2. Extend the CI matrix to the range composer claims:
   ```yaml
   php-versions: ['8.2', '8.3', '8.4', '8.5']
   ```
3. Raise `vimeo/psalm` to `^6` and `ergebnis/composer-normalize` to a release supporting 8.4/8.5,
   or narrow `"php"` to `>=8.2 <8.4` and say so in README.md:47. Advertising `^8.2` while the
   toolchain caps at 8.3 is the drift to resolve either way.

## Resolution
All implicit-nullable params made explicit (?bool/?Type). Deprecations 17 -> 0 on PHP 8.5. CI matrix extended to 8.2/8.3/8.4/8.5. psalm ^6 and composer-normalize ^2.47 now install cleanly on 8.5 without --ignore-platform-req.
title: 17 PHP 8.4+ deprecations in src, and the CI matrix never tests the PHP versions composer allows

## Problem

`composer audit` reports two advisories against the committed lock file. Both are dev-only, but
`require-dev` includes `roave/security-advisories: dev-latest`, whose entire purpose is to make
installing a known-vulnerable version impossible — a locked tree that still resolves to vulnerable
versions means the lock has not been refreshed since the advisories were published.

## Evidence

```
$ composer audit --format=summary
Found 2 security vulnerability advisories affecting 2 packages.

$ composer audit | grep '^| Package'
| Package | phpunit/phpunit  |
| Package | symfony/process  |

$ composer audit --no-dev
No security vulnerability advisories found.
```

- `phpunit/phpunit` — locked at 10.5.30; advisory affects `>=10.0.0,<10.5.62`, reported 2026-01-27.
- `symfony/process` — CVE-2024-51736, command execution hijack on Windows, reported 2024-11-05,
  fixed in 6.4.14 (transitive, via the dev toolchain).

Runtime dependencies are clean: `composer licenses --no-dev` lists only `psr/container` and
`symfony/*`, all MIT, all advisory-free.

## Impact

Dev-only, so no consumer of the published package is exposed. The exposure is to contributors and
CI: `symfony/process` CVE-2024-51736 is a command-execution hijack that fires on Windows
development machines, and the CI workflow runs `composer install` unpinned against this lock on
every push.

## Fix

```
composer update phpunit/phpunit symfony/process --with-all-dependencies
composer audit
```

and add `composer audit` as a gating CI step so a lock file with published advisories fails the
build rather than sitting unnoticed:

```yaml
- name: Security audit
  run: composer audit
```

Renovate is already configured (renovate.json) — confirm its config enables `vulnerabilityAlerts`
so lock refreshes are proposed automatically.

## Resolution
composer update refreshed the lock (phpunit 10.5.30 -> 10.5.64, psalm 5.25 -> 6.16.1, symfony/process resolved). composer audit now reports no advisories, and is a gating CI step.
title: composer.lock is stale: two dev dependencies carry published advisories despite roave/security-advisories

body:
## Problem

`Reflector::translateVisibilityFilter()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php:131-141) maps
four known filters and silently defaults everything else to `IS_PUBLIC`:

```php
$map = [
    'public'    => ReflectionMethod::IS_PUBLIC,
    'protected' => ReflectionMethod::IS_PROTECTED,
    'abstract'  => ReflectionMethod::IS_ABSTRACT,
    'final'     => ReflectionMethod::IS_FINAL,
];

return $map[$filter] ?? ReflectionMethod::IS_PUBLIC;
```

`--visibility` is a free-text comma-separated option (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:71-77)
with no validation at the CLI boundary either.

## Evidence

`--visibility=private` is neither rejected nor honoured: `'private'` misses the map, falls through
to `IS_PUBLIC`, and the command emits the public API. `--visibility=publi` (a typo) behaves
identically. In both cases exit code is 0 and no diagnostic is written.

`private` is in fact unsupported by design — `Reflector::shouldIgnoreFunction()` (line 210-218)
excludes `$method->isPrivate()` unconditionally — but nothing tells the user that.

## Impact

A typo or an unsupported visibility produces plausible-looking but wrong documentation with no
signal that the request was ignored. This is a fail-open default on the one option that controls
what the tool includes.

## Fix

Validate at the boundary and reject unknown values:

```php
private const VISIBILITIES = [
    'public'    => ReflectionMethod::IS_PUBLIC,
    'protected' => ReflectionMethod::IS_PROTECTED,
    'abstract'  => ReflectionMethod::IS_ABSTRACT,
    'final'     => ReflectionMethod::IS_FINAL,
];

private function translateVisibilityFilter(string $filter): int
{
    if (!isset(self::VISIBILITIES[$filter])) {
        throw new InvalidArgumentException(sprintf(
            'Unknown visibility "%s". Supported: %s',
            $filter,
            implode(', ', array_keys(self::VISIBILITIES))
        ));
    }

    return self::VISIBILITIES[$filter];
}
```

Document in README.md that `private` is not supported, and add a test asserting an unknown
visibility exits non-zero with that message.

## Resolution
translateVisibilityFilter() throws InvalidArgumentException naming the supported values instead of silently defaulting to IS_PUBLIC; map extracted to a VISIBILITIES const. Covered by testUnknownVisibilityFilterIsRejected. README documents that private is unsupported.
title: Unknown --visibility values silently fall back to public instead of failing

## Problem

Five declarations have zero call sites in the entire repository.

| Declaration | Location | Callers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Utils::getSanitizedTypeDeclaration()` (private) | src/PHPDocsMD/Utils.php:104 | none — its body is duplicated inline at Utils.php:78 and :106 |
| `ClassEntity::isNative()` + `$isNative` field | src/PHPDocsMD/Entities/ClassEntity.php:25, 41 | never read or written |
| `FunctionEntity::setTodo()` / `getTodo()` + `$todo` field | src/PHPDocsMD/Entities/FunctionEntity.php:22, 140, 146 | never called; `@todo` is not extracted by `DocInfoExtractor` |
| `DocInfo::getParameters()` | src/PHPDocsMD/DocInfo.php:33 | never called (`getParameterInfo()` is used instead) |
| `guessReturnTypeFromFuncName()` `$name === 'self'` branch | src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php:253-255 | unreachable — `$name` is always a method name (see the `@return self` finding) |

`MDTableGenerator::appendExamplesToEndOfTable()` (src/PHPDocsMD/MDTableGenerator.php:37) is a
distinct case: it is part of the published `TableGenerator` interface but the command never calls
it, so the behaviour it toggles is not reachable from the CLI.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -rn 'getSanitizedTypeDeclaration' src test bin
src/PHPDocsMD/Utils.php:104:    private static function getSanitizedTypeDeclaration(...)

$ grep -rn 'setTodo\|getTodo' src test bin
src/PHPDocsMD/Entities/FunctionEntity.php:140:    public function setTodo(...)
src/PHPDocsMD/Entities/FunctionEntity.php:146:    public function getTodo(...)
```

Same result for `isNative` (only its own declaration and backing field) and
`DocInfo::getParameters`.

## Impact

A private method with no callers is a latent bug: a PSR-2 run does not flag it, and a reader
assumes `getSanitizedTypeDeclaration()` is the canonical sanitiser when in fact two hand-copied
duplicates of it are what actually run. `setTodo`/`getTodo` advertise a `@todo` feature the
extractor never populates.

## Fix

Delete `Utils::getSanitizedTypeDeclaration()` — or better, keep it and route Utils.php:78 and :106
through it, removing the duplication. Delete `ClassEntity::isNative()` and `$isNative`,
`FunctionEntity::setTodo()`/`getTodo()`/`$todo`, `DocInfo::getParameters()`, and the unreachable
`self` branch in `guessReturnTypeFromFuncName()`.

Then flip psalm to catch the next one: set `findUnusedCode="true"` in psalm.xml (currently
`"false"`, psalm.xml:9) and wire `composer psalm` into CI. Either call
`appendExamplesToEndOfTable()` from the command behind a new option, or drop it from the interface.

## Resolution
Removed Utils::getSanitizedTypeDeclaration duplication by routing isClassReference() through it, deleted ClassEntity::isNative()+field, FunctionEntity::setTodo/getTodo+field, DocInfo::getParameters(), and the unreachable self branch in guessReturnTypeFromFuncName(). findUnusedCode was NOT enabled - see the note on audit-9fc57d49.
title: Dead code: five members with no callers anywhere in src, test or bin

body:
## Problem

Two packaging issues in composer.json:

**Hardcoded `version`.** composer.json:5 declares `"version": "4.0.0"`. Composer explicitly
discourages this for packages published via VCS — the version is inferred from the git tag, and a
hardcoded field silently disagrees with it after any release where the bump is forgotten.
`CLI::__construct()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/CLI.php:21-27) reads this field and reports it as the
application version, so `phpdoc-md --version` prints whatever is in the file, not what is
installed.

**PSR-0 autoloading.** composer.json `autoload` uses `"psr-0": {"PHPDocsMD": "src/"}`, and
`autoload-dev` uses `"psr-0": {"Acme\\": "test/"}`. PSR-0 was deprecated by PHP-FIG in 2014 in
favour of PSR-4; composer still honours it but generates a slower classmap fallback for it.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -n '"version"\|psr-0' composer.json
5:    "version": "4.0.0",
     "psr-0": { "PHPDocsMD": "src/" }
     "psr-0": { "Acme\\": "test/" }

$ git log --oneline | head -6      # last release commit
d5a11dc 4.0.0
```

Five commits have landed on `main` since the `4.0.0` commit — including one marked
`chore(deps)!:` with a breaking-change bang — while composer.json still reports `4.0.0`. There is
no CHANGELOG.md to reconcile against.

## Impact

`phpdoc-md --version` is unreliable, and the declared version cannot be trusted as a semver signal
by consumers. The `chore(deps)!:` bang on commit 888bfa5 is itself overstated — that commit bumps
a GitHub Action SHA in CI, which has no effect on the published package's public API and should
not carry a breaking-change marker.

## Fix

1. Remove `"version": "4.0.0"` from composer.json and let the git tag be authoritative. Change
   `CLI::__construct()` to source the version from `Composer\InstalledVersions`:
   ```php
   parent::__construct(
       'PHP Markdown Documentation Generator',
       \Composer\InstalledVersions::getPrettyVersion('ivuorinen/markdowndocs') ?? 'dev'
   );
   ```
   This also removes the `file_get_contents` + `json_decode` on a path relative to `__DIR__`, and
   with it the `ext-json` requirement's only use.
2. Migrate to PSR-4:
   ```json
   "autoload":     { "psr-4": { "PHPDocsMD\\": "src/PHPDocsMD/" } },
   "autoload-dev": { "psr-4": { "Acme\\": "test/Acme/" } }
   ```
   Note `test/Acme/ExampleClass.php` declares several classes in one file, which PSR-4 does not
   support — split it, or keep a `classmap` entry for the fixture directory.
3. Reserve `!` / `BREAKING CHANGE` for commits that change the package's public API.

## Resolution
Removed the hardcoded version; CLI resolves it from Composer\InstalledVersions (--version now prints dev-main rather than a stale 4.0.0). Dropped ext-json, which only json_decode of composer.json needed. Migrated autoload and autoload-dev to PSR-4. symfony/console widened to ^5||^6||^7.
title: composer.json pins a hardcoded version the CLI reads at runtime, and autoloads via deprecated PSR-0

body:
## Problem

Three quality gates are configured and none of them is effective:

- phpcs.xml:4 sets `<file>src</file>`. `test/` (595 lines) and `bin/phpdoc-md` are never linted.
- psalm.xml:12 scopes `<directory name="src" />` only, at `errorLevel="5"` (the loosest of psalm's
  1-8 scale, where 1 is strictest) with `findUnusedCode="false"`.
- Neither `composer lint` nor `composer psalm` is invoked by any workflow — see the separate
  finding on `.github/workflows/php.yml`.

Type declarations in `src` also contradict their own docblocks:

```php
/**
 * @return \PHPDocsMD\Entities\FunctionEntity|true      // src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php:178
 */
private function findInheritedFunctionDeclaration(...): FunctionEntity|bool
```

The method returns `FunctionEntity` or throws; it never returns `true`. `createFunctionEntity()`
(line 146-150) declares `bool|FunctionEntity` and returns `false`, not `true`. At `errorLevel="5"`
psalm does not flag either.

## Evidence

```
$ vendor/bin/phpcs
................ 16 / 16 (100%)     # 16 files — src only; test/ and bin/ absent

$ grep -rn 'phpcs\|psalm' .github/workflows/
(no run steps)
```

Psalm additionally crashes outright on PHP 8.5 (`vimeo/psalm ^5` predates it), so even a manual
`composer psalm` produces no analysis on a current interpreter — recorded here as *errored*, not
clean.

## Impact

Nothing enforces the standards the repo declares. The `@return ...|true` docblocks are wrong in a
project whose entire output is generated from docblocks — the tool's own `docs.md` publishes
`FunctionEntity | bool` for these methods.

## Fix

1. Widen phpcs.xml to the whole tree:
   ```xml
   <file>src</file>
   <file>test</file>
   <file>bin</file>
   ```
2. Add `test` to psalm.xml `<projectFiles>`, drop `errorLevel` to `3` (or lower) once the resulting
   findings are triaged, and set `findUnusedCode="true"`.
3. Fix the two contradicting docblocks: `@return FunctionEntity` on
   `findInheritedFunctionDeclaration()` and `@return FunctionEntity|false` on
   `createFunctionEntity()`.
4. Upgrade `vimeo/psalm` to `^6` so it runs at all on the PHP versions composer claims to support.

## Resolution
psalm upgraded 5.25 -> 6.16.1 (it no longer crashes on PHP 8.5) and both phpcs and psalm are now gating CI steps. phpcs widened to src+bin. All 20 psalm errors resolved to zero: fixed InvalidReturnType/InvalidReturnStatement by narrowing FunctionFinder::find/findInClasses to FunctionEntity|false, InvalidNullableReturnType/NullableReturnStatement in getParamType via ?? '' (and preg_quote on the interpolated param name), InvalidArgument on the new ksort, and added 15 #[\Override] attributes. Corrected the two contradicting docblocks. Two of this finding's recommendations were deliberately NOT applied - see the follow-up finding on linter scope.
title: Static analysis and linting cover src only, at the loosest settings, and neither runs anywhere automatically

## Problem

`composer.json` declares `"php": "^8.2"` and the CI matrix runs `8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5`, but the
committed `composer.lock` pins packages that require `php >=8.4.1`. There is no
`config.platform.php` in composer.json, so `composer update` resolves against whatever PHP the
maintainer happens to be running — here PHP 8.5 — and writes a lock that cannot be installed on
the older half of the supported range.

The offending constraint reaches the **runtime** tree, not just dev:

| Section | Package | Locked | Requires |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| packages | symfony/string | v8.1.2 | `php >=8.4.1` |
| packages-dev | symfony/event-dispatcher, filesystem, finder, options-resolver, process, stopwatch | v8.1.x | `php >=8.4.1` |

`symfony/string` is pulled in by `symfony/console` v7.4.15, whose own constraint
`symfony/string: ^7.2|^8.0` allowed the resolver to take the 8.x line.

## Evidence

```
$ php8.2 $(command -v composer) install --dry-run
  Problem 3
    - symfony/filesystem is locked to version v8.1.2 ... requires php >=8.4.1
      -> your php version (8.2.32) does not satisfy that requirement.
  ...
  Problem 8
    - symfony/console is locked to version v7.4.15 ...
    - symfony/console v7.4.15 requires symfony/string ^7.2|^8.0 -> satisfiable by symfony/string[v8.1.2].
    - symfony/string v8.1.2 requires php >=8.4.1 -> your php version (8.2.32) does not satisfy that requirement.
```

Eight resolution problems, zero installable. PHP 8.3 fails identically (8.3 < 8.4.1).

## Impact
- `.github/workflows/php.yml` runs `composer install` on the `8.2` and `8.3` matrix legs — both
  fail at the install step, so **2 of 4 legs are red** and the workflow (now correctly gating
  after the previous audit removed `continue-on-error`) blocks every merge.
- A contributor on PHP 8.2 or 8.3 cannot set the project up at all.

Consumers of the published package are *not* affected: a library's `composer.lock` is ignored
downstream, so `composer require ivuorinen/markdowndocs` on PHP 8.2 resolves `symfony/console`
freshly and correctly. The breakage is confined to development and CI — which is why this is High
and not Critical.

This is a regression introduced by the `composer update` run during the previous audit in this
same session; the lock before that run predated `symfony/string` 8.x.

## Fix

Pin the resolution target to the **minimum** supported PHP so the lock is installable across the
entire declared range, then re-lock:

```json
"config": {
    "allow-plugins": {
        "ergebnis/composer-normalize": true
    },
    "platform": {
        "php": "8.2.0"
    }
}
```

```
composer update --no-interaction
php8.2 $(command -v composer) install --dry-run   # must succeed
```

`config.platform.php` must be kept in lockstep with `require.php`: raising the floor to 8.3 later
means changing both. Add a CI guard so the two cannot drift — the matrix already covers 8.2, and
with the platform pinned the `composer install` step on that leg is itself the check.

## Resolution
Added config.platform.php. Pinned to 8.2.27 rather than 8.2.0: psalm 6 requires ~8.2.27, so an 8.2.0 pin made the graph unresolvable and composer update failed outright. Re-locked - symfony/string, event-dispatcher, filesystem, finder, options-resolver, process and stopwatch all downgraded 8.1.x -> 7.4.x. Verified: composer install --dry-run OK on 8.2/8.3/8.4/8.5, and no locked package rejects the 8.2 line.
title: composer.lock is only installable on PHP >=8.4, so half the declared and CI-tested range cannot build

body:
## Problem

`phpunit.xml` sets no `failOnDeprecation`, `failOnWarning` or `failOnNotice`. PHPUnit reports
deprecations and then exits successfully, so CI stays green while the code accumulates
deprecations on newer PHP branches.

This is precisely how the 17 implicit-nullable deprecations fixed in the previous audit accrued
unnoticed: they were invisible on the 8.2/8.3 legs the matrix ran, and nothing would have failed
even had a newer leg existed.

## Evidence

Reintroducing a single deprecation into a scratch copy of the current tree:

```
$ sed -i 's/isStatic(?bool $toggle = null)/isStatic(bool $toggle = null)/' src/PHPDocsMD/Entities/FunctionEntity.php
$ vendor/bin/phpunit
OK, but there were issues!
Tests: 54, Assertions: 202, Deprecations: 1.

$ vendor/bin/phpunit >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?
0
```

Exit code 0. "OK, but there were issues!" is not a failure, and CI reads only the exit code.

## Impact

"Supports all currently supported PHP versions" is unenforceable without this. The matrix can run
8.2 through 8.5 and still report success while every method signature is deprecated on the newest
branch — which is exactly the state the project was in before the previous audit.

## Fix

Make deprecations fail the build:

```xml
<phpunit
        xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
        xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://schema.phpunit.de/10.5/phpunit.xsd"
        bootstrap="vendor/autoload.php"
        colors="true"
        cacheDirectory=".phpunit.cache"
        failOnDeprecation="true"
        failOnNotice="true"
        failOnWarning="true"
>
```

The suite currently reports 0 deprecations on PHP 8.5, so this can be turned on today without a
grace period. If a dependency later emits a deprecation the project cannot fix, silence that one
source with `<source><deprecationTrigger>` rather than disabling the flag.

## Resolution
phpunit.xml now sets failOnDeprecation, failOnNotice and failOnWarning to true. Re-ran the scratch reproduction (one implicit-nullable param reintroduced): exit code went 0 -> 1. Current tree reports 0 deprecations on all four supported versions, so no grace period was needed.
title: PHPUnit exits 0 when PHP emits deprecations, so a new PHP branch degrades support silently

body:
## Problem

`require.symfony/console` is `^5 || ^6 || ^7`. Symfony 8 is excluded, so any project that has
already moved to `symfony/console` 8 cannot install this package at all — composer refuses the
conflict.

Symfony 8 requires `php >=8.4.1`, i.e. it is the current line for two of the four supported PHP
branches (8.4 and 8.5). Widening the constraint alone is not enough: the code calls a method
Symfony 8 removed.

`CLI::run()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/CLI.php) calls `$this->add(new PHPDocsMDCommand())`.
`Application::add()` was deprecated in Symfony 7.4 and deleted in 8.0, replaced by
`Application::addCommand()`.

## Evidence

Installing the current sources against `symfony/console: ^8` on PHP 8.5:

```
$ composer show symfony/console
versions : * v8.1.2

$ vendor/bin/phpunit
ERRORS!
Tests: 54, Assertions: 187, Errors: 7.

$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate src
phpdoc-md: Call to undefined method PHPDocsMD\Console\CLI::add()

$ ./bin/phpdoc-md --version
phpdoc-md: Call to undefined method PHPDocsMD\Console\CLI::add()
```

The method is genuinely gone from the class:

```
$ grep -n 'function add\b\|function addCommand' vendor/symfony/console/Application.php
578:    public function addCommands(array $commands): void
591:    public function addCommand(callable|Command $command): ?Command
```

Every entry point fails — the CLI is completely non-functional, not merely degraded.

## Impact

The tool is unusable in any project on the current Symfony line. Because `phpdoc-md` is installed
as a dev dependency *into the consumer's project*, a single incompatible constraint blocks the
whole install; the consumer cannot work around it.

## Fix

Widen the constraint and add a shim that works across the whole range. `addCommand()` exists from
Symfony 7.4 onward; `add()` exists up to 7.x:

```json
"symfony/console": "^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8"
```

```php
#[\Override]
public function run(?InputInterface $input = null, ?OutputInterface $output = null): int
{
    $command = new PHPDocsMDCommand();

    // Application::add() was removed in Symfony 8; addCommand() arrived in 7.4.
    if (method_exists($this, 'addCommand')) {
        $this->addCommand($command);
    } else {
        $this->add($command);
    }

    return parent::run($input, $output);
}
```

Then add a CI leg that resolves the newest allowed dependencies on PHP 8.5
(`composer update --prefer-stable`) so the Symfony 8 path is actually exercised, not merely
permitted — the pinned `config.platform.php` means the default lock will always take Symfony 7.

## Resolution
Widened symfony/console to ^5 || ^6 || ^7 || ^8 and added a method_exists('addCommand') shim in CLI::run() and in PHPDocsMDCommandTest::setUp() (the test called the removed add() directly, which accounted for all 7 errors after the src fix). Verified against symfony/console v8.1.2 on PHP 8.5: 54 tests / 202 assertions pass and the CLI generates docs. A dedicated 'highest' CI leg on PHP 8.5 unsets platform.php and runs composer update, so the Symfony 8 path is exercised - the pinned lock always resolves Symfony 7 and would otherwise never reach it.
title: Package cannot be installed alongside symfony/console 8, the natural choice on PHP 8.4 and 8.5

body:
## Problem

README.md's Requirements section reads:

> - PHP version >= 8.2

That is a floor with no ceiling and no statement of what is actually tested. A reader on PHP 8.5
cannot tell whether the project supports their version deliberately or incidentally, and a reader
on PHP 8.1 (end-of-life since 31 Dec 2025) is not told their version is unsupported.

The composer constraint `^8.2` in fact excludes 9.x, so an upper bound does exist and is simply
undocumented.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -A5 '### Requirements' README.md
- PHP version >= 8.2
- Reflection must be enabled in php.ini
...
```

Against php.net's supported-versions table as of 2026-08-02:

| Branch | Status |
| --- | --- |
| 8.2 | security fixes only (until 31 Dec 2026) |
| 8.3 | active support |
| 8.4 | active support |
| 8.5 | active support |

8.1 and earlier are end-of-life. So the honest statement is "8.2 through 8.5", matching both
`^8.2` and the CI matrix.

## Impact

Minor, but it is the only place a consumer looks before installing, and it is the sentence that
should be updated whenever the floor moves.

## Fix

State the range and where it is enforced:

```markdown
### Requirements

- PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 — every branch currently supported by php.net. Each is exercised by CI
  on every push.
- Reflection must be enabled in php.ini
- Each class must be defined in its own file with the file name being the same as the class name
- The project should use [Composer](https://getcomposer.org/)
```

Keep this list, `require.php`, `config.platform.php` and the CI matrix in agreement — they are
four statements of the same fact.

## Resolution
README Requirements now reads 'PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 or 8.5 - every branch currently supported by php.net. Each one is exercised by CI on every push.' Matches require.php (^8.2), config.platform.php (8.2.27) and the CI matrix.
title: README states a PHP floor but never the supported or tested range

body:
## Problem

`psalm.xml` sets no `phpVersion` attribute. Psalm then analyses against the version of PHP running
it, so the same source is checked as 8.2 on the CI 8.2 leg, as 8.5 on the 8.5 leg, and as whatever
a maintainer happens to have locally. Version-sensitive analysis — `#[\Override]` enforcement,
readonly semantics, union and DNF type handling — can therefore disagree between environments.

## Evidence

There is **no divergence today**. Both targets are clean on the current tree:

```
$ vendor/bin/psalm --php-version=8.2 ; vendor/bin/psalm --php-version=8.5
No errors found
No errors found
```

So this is a preventive configuration gap, not a live defect, and it is filed Low on that basis.
The mechanism is real — `--php-version` demonstrably drives the analysis and its default is the
running interpreter — but no current failing scenario exists to construct.

## Impact

With the CI matrix now spanning 8.2 to 8.5, psalm runs four times against four different targets.
When they eventually disagree, the failure appears on one matrix leg only and reads as a flake
rather than as a deliberate version difference.

## Fix

Pin the analysis target to the supported floor, matching `require.php` and `config.platform.php`:

```xml
<psalm
    errorLevel="5"
    phpVersion="8.2"
    ...
>
```

Analysing at the floor is the right default: it catches use of syntax or semantics unavailable on
the oldest supported branch, which is the failure mode that actually matters for a package
claiming `^8.2`.

## Resolution
psalm.xml now sets phpVersion="8.2", pinning analysis to the supported floor so all five CI legs and any local run agree. Confirmed still 'No errors found' on 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5.
title: psalm has no phpVersion, so its analysis target is whichever PHP happens to invoke it

body: ## Problem `MDTableGenerator::stripCodeTags()` detected the opening tag with a **prefix** test but split on the **literal** tag: ```php if (str_contains($example, ' $parts = array_slice(explode('', $example), -2); $example = (string)current($parts); $parts = array_slice(explode('', $example), 1); // finds nothing $example = (string)current($parts); // current([]) === false -> '' } ``` With any attribute on the tag the second `explode` produces no element after the delimiter, `current()` on the empty array returns `false`, and the cast turns the whole example into an empty string. The example is not degraded — it is deleted. ## Evidence ``` $ php -r '... echo PHPDocsMD\MDTableGenerator::formatExampleComment("\n \$x = 1;\n");' ``` ``` ``` Empty fenced block. The bare-tag form worked: ``` $ ... formatExampleComment("\n \$x = 1;\n") ``` $x = 1; ``` ``` Found while writing coverage for this class, which was at 59.5% with `formatExampleComment` and `stripCodeTags` entirely untested. ## Impact Any `@example` block written as ``, `` or similar loses its entire body in the generated documentation, with no warning and no visible trace beyond an empty code fence. The project's own docblocks use the bare form, so it never bit here. ## Fix Match the opening tag as a pattern so attributes are tolerated, and keep the existing "last complete block wins" semantics: ```php private static function stripCodeTags(string $example): string { if (!str_contains($example, ']*>(.*?)#s', $example, $matches); $blocks = $matches[1]; if ($blocks !== []) { return (string)end($blocks); } // Opening tag with no closing tag: keep everything after it. return (string)preg_replace('#^.*?]*>#s', '', $example); } ``` Covered by `MDTableGeneratorTest::testCodeTagsAreStripped`, which data-provides the bare tag, a `class` attribute, multiple attributes, two blocks, and an unclosed tag. ## Resolution Fixed as described; MDTableGenerator coverage went 59.5% -> 100%. The (string)end() cast is deliberate: end() is falsable on an empty array and psalm flagged it, so the non-empty case is now explicit.
title: stripCodeTags() silently discards any @example wrapped in a <code> tag carrying attributes

body: ## Problem `findClassInFile()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php:340) recognises only two declaration keywords: ```php } elseif (str_contains($line, 'class')) { $class = $this->extractClassNameFromLine('class', $line); break; } elseif (str_contains($line, 'interface')) { $class = $this->extractClassNameFromLine('interface', $line); break; } ``` There is no `trait` or `enum` branch, so for a trait or enum file the loop runs off the end, `$class` stays `false`, and the file is dropped with no diagnostic. `execute()` (line 134) is explicit that both are supported inputs: ```php if (class_exists($class) || interface_exists($class) || trait_exists($class)) { ``` `class_exists()` returns true for enums, and `trait_exists()` is checked by name. So a trait or enum passed as the `class` argument is documented, but the same file inside a scanned directory is invisible. The directory path is the documented primary workflow (`phpdoc-md generate src > api.md`). ## Evidence Fixture: `Probe\MyTrait` (a trait) and `Probe\MyEnum` (a backed enum), both autoloaded via `--bootstrap`, in a directory alongside two interfaces and two classes. ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate 'Probe\MyTrait' -b bootstrap.php ### Class: \Probe\MyTrait | public | hello() : string | $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate 'Probe\MyEnum' -b bootstrap.php ### Class: \Probe\MyEnum | public static | cases() : array | ... $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate ./Src -b bootstrap.php | grep -c 'MyTrait\|MyEnum' 0 ``` The same two types documented fine by name, and absent entirely from the directory scan. The table of contents lists only `\Probe\Aye`, `\Probe\Because`, `\Probe\Bee`, `\Probe\Shapes`. ## Impact Any codebase that uses traits or enums gets an API document that silently omits them. There is no warning, no exit code, and no entry in the table of contents — the omission is indistinguishable from the type not existing. Enums have been idiomatic PHP since 8.1 and this package requires PHP >= 8.2. ## Fix Extend the keyword list in `findClassInFile()`, and match on a declaration keyword rather than a substring (see the related finding on `str_contains($line, 'class')` false positives): ```php foreach (['class', 'interface', 'trait', 'enum'] as $keyword) { if (preg_match('/^\s*(?:(?:final|abstract|readonly)\s+)*' . $keyword . '\s+(\w+)/', $line, $m)) { $class = $m[1]; break 2; } } ``` Add a fixture trait and enum under `test/Acme/Fixtures/Tree/` and assert both appear in `PHPDocsMDCommandTest`. ## Resolution findClassInFile() now tokenises with token_get_all() and accepts T_CLASS/T_INTERFACE/T_TRAIT/T_ENUM. Regression: PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testEveryDeclarationKindIsDiscovered over new fixtures test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/{PlainClass,PlainTrait,PlainEnum}.php.
title: Traits and enums are silently skipped when a directory is scanned, though both work when named explicitly

body: ## Problem `Reflector::getParamType()` (src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php:433) exempts exactly one native type from namespace prefixing: ```php if ($type !== 'array' && !str_starts_with($type, '\\')) { $type = '\\' . $type; } ``` `bool`, `string`, `int`, `float`, `void`, `callable`, `iterable`, `mixed` are all treated as class references and get a leading `\`. `Utils::$nativeTypes` already enumerates the full set; this call site does not consult it. When a parameter carries no `@param` docblock, `createParameterEntity()` takes the declared type verbatim as `$docs['type']`, so the mangled value reaches the rendered table. ## Evidence Direct call: ``` $ php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; $m = new ReflectionMethod(PHPDocsMD\MDTableGenerator::class, "addFunc"); foreach ($m->getParameters() as $p) { printf("%-12s -> %s\n", $p->getName(), Reflector::getParamType($p)); }' func -> \PHPDocsMD\Entities\FunctionEntity includeSee -> \bool ``` The defect is present in this project's own committed API reference: ``` $ grep -o '\\bool\|\\string' docs.md | sort | uniq -c 6 \bool 2 \string docs.md: | public | appendExamplesToEndOfTable(\bool $toggle) : void | docs.md: | public | doDeclareAbstraction(\bool $toggle) : void | docs.md: | public | addFunc(... \bool $includeSee=false) | ``` An enum shows the same through a different route — `BackedEnum::from(string|int $value)` renders as `\int`. ## Impact Every parameter whose type comes only from the PHP signature — the common case for code without `@param` tags, which the README explicitly advertises as supported ("functions that are missing DocBlock comments will still be included") — renders with a bogus leading backslash. `\bool` is not a valid type reference; readers of the generated document see a broken type. It is visible right now in this repository's published `docs.md`. ## Fix Consult the existing native-type list instead of special-casing `array`: ```php if (!Utils::isNativeType($type) && !str_starts_with($type, '\\')) { $type = '\\' . $type; } ``` `Utils::isNativeType()` already trims a leading backslash and lowercases, so it is correct for the values `getParamType()` produces. Add a `ReflectorTest` case asserting that a method declared `fn(bool $a, string $b, int $c)` with no docblock yields types `bool`, `string`, `int`, then regenerate `docs.md`. ## Resolution getParamType() now reads ReflectionParameter::getType() through the new Reflector::formatReflectionType(), which renders native types bare. docs.md regenerated: zero \bool/\string cells remain. Regression: ReflectorTest::testNativeParameterTypesAreNotTreatedAsClassReferences.
title: getParamType() prefixes every native scalar with a backslash, so parameters render as \bool and \string

body: ## Problem `getReturnTypeFromMethod()` handles `ReflectionUnionType` and `ReflectionNamedType`, but not `ReflectionIntersectionType` (PHP 8.1+, and this package requires PHP >= 8.2): ```php $name = $method->getReturnType(); if ($name instanceof ReflectionUnionType) { ... } $name = ($name === null || !method_exists($name, 'getName')) ? $returnType : $name->getName(); ``` `ReflectionIntersectionType` has no `getName()`, so `$name` falls back to `$returnType`, which is `''` when there is no `@return` docblock. `Utils::isNativeType('')` is false, so the else branch builds `'\\' . ''` — a lone backslash. That string is then passed to `class_exists()`: ```php private function classExists(string $classRef): bool { return class_exists(trim($classRef, '[]')); // class_exists('\') } ``` ## Evidence ```php public function intersection(): Aye&Bee { ... } ``` ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate ./Src -b bootstrap.php PHP Warning: Uninitialized string offset 0 in vendor/composer/ClassLoader.php on line 497 PHP Stack trace: ... #13 PHPDocsMD\Reflections\Reflector->classExists($classRef = '\') Reflector.php:251 #14 class_exists($class = '\') Reflector.php:281 #16 Composer\Autoload\ClassLoader->findFile($class = '') | public | intersection() : | ``` Two defects in one line: an empty return-type cell, and a PHP warning on stderr originating inside Composer's autoloader. ## Impact Documentation for intersection-typed methods is wrong (blank rather than `\Aye & \Bee`), and the warning pollutes stderr for anyone running the generator in a CI docs pipeline — with `display_errors` on, as the stack trace above shows, it is many lines per occurrence. ## Fix Handle the intersection case alongside the union case, and guard `classExists()`: ```php if ($name instanceof ReflectionUnionType || $name instanceof \ReflectionIntersectionType) { $glue = $name instanceof ReflectionUnionType ? '|' : '&'; $returnType = implode($glue, array_map(static fn($t) => $t->getName(), $name->getTypes())); $name = null; } ``` and ```php private function classExists(string $classRef): bool { $classRef = trim($classRef, '[]\\'); return $classRef !== '' && class_exists($classRef); } ``` `Utils::sanitizeDeclaration()` takes a `$delimiter` argument already, so the `&` form can be sanitised with `sanitizeDeclaration($returnType, $ns, '&')`. Add a `ReflectorTest` fixture method with an intersection return type. ## Resolution formatReflectionType() handles ReflectionIntersectionType recursively and joins with ' & '; classExists() now rejects an empty reference instead of passing '\' to the autoloader. Intersection renders '\A & \B' and stderr is clean. Regression: ReflectorTest::testReturnTypeShapesSurviveIntact.
title: Intersection return types render as an empty cell and emit a PHP warning to stderr

body: ## Problem `Utils::isNativeType()` normalises away a leading backslash before its lookup: ```php $type = strtolower(trim($type)); $type = trim($type, '\\'); return in_array($type, self::$nativeTypes, true); ``` `Utils::getSanitizedTypeDeclaration()` — the helper `isClassReference()` uses — does not: ```php private static function getSanitizedTypeDeclaration(string $typeDeclaration): string { return strtolower(rtrim(trim($typeDeclaration), '[]')); } ``` So the two functions disagree: `\string` is a native type *and* a class reference. `Reflector::getReturnTypeFromMethod()` produces exactly such a value for union return types. It implodes the union members, then tests the whole joined string against `isNativeType()`: ```php if ($name !== 'self' && Utils::isNativeType($name)) { // "string|int" -> false $returnType = $name; } else { $returnType = $name === 'self' ? '\\' . $method->class : '\\' . $name; // "\string|int" } ``` `sanitizeDeclaration()` then splits on `|`, and `isClassReference('\string')` returns true, so the first member is kept as a class reference. ## Evidence ``` $ php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; use PHPDocsMD\Utils; var_dump(Utils::isNativeType("\\string"), Utils::isClassReference("\\string")); var_dump(Utils::sanitizeDeclaration("\\string|int", ""));' bool(true) bool(true) string(13) "\string | int" ``` End to end, for `public function unionNative(): string|int`: ``` | public | unionNative() : \string \| int | ``` `\string` is wrong; `string` is correct. ## Impact Every union return type made of native types renders its first member as a bogus class reference. The asymmetry is also a latent trap for any future caller of `isClassReference()`: the function answers "yes, a class" for `\int`, `\bool`, `\array`. ## Fix Make the two helpers normalise identically: ```php private static function getSanitizedTypeDeclaration(string $typeDeclaration): string { return trim(strtolower(rtrim(trim($typeDeclaration), '[]')), '\\'); } ``` `UtilsTest::testNativeTypesAreNeverTreatedAsClasses` already iterates `Utils::$nativeTypes`; extend its data provider to feed each type twice, bare and backslash-prefixed. That test fails today for the prefixed form. ## Resolution Utils::getSanitizedTypeDeclaration() now trims the leading backslash exactly as isNativeType() does, so the two helpers agree. The visible symptom is gone at source too: getReturnTypeFromMethod() no longer builds '\string|int'. unionNative() renders 'string | int'.
title: isClassReference() does not strip a leading backslash, so native union return types render as \string | int
UseInspector splits on the substring 'use' anywhere in a file, so aliased and grouped imports never resolve

body: ## Problem `getReturnTypeFromMethod()` reads `ReflectionNamedType::getName()`, which returns the type without its nullability marker. `ReflectionNamedType::allowsNull()` is never consulted: ```php $name = ($name === null || !method_exists($name, 'getName')) ? $returnType : $name->getName(); ``` The same holds on the parameter side: `getParamType()` derives the type from `(string) $refParam` after stripping `' or NULL'`: ```php $export = str_replace(' or NULL', '', (string)$refParam); ``` so the nullability is deliberately discarded there too. ## Evidence ```php class Shapes { public function nullableObj(): ?Aye { return null; } public function nullableScalar(): ?string { return null; } } ``` ``` | public | nullableObj() : [\Probe\Aye](#interface-probeaye) | | public | nullableScalar() : string | ``` Both cells claim the method always returns a value. The correct renderings are `\Probe\Aye | null` and `string | null`. Note the generator already knows how to render nullability: `Foo|null` written as an explicit union comes through `ReflectionUnionType` and renders as `\Foo | null`. So `?Foo` and `Foo|null` — the same type in PHP — document differently. ## Impact A caller reading the generated docs for `nullableObj()` will not null-check the result. Nullable returns are extremely common (finders, lookups, optional getters), so this understates the contract across most real codebases, and it does so inconsistently with the union form. ## Fix Append `null` when reflection says the type admits it, in `getReturnTypeFromMethod()`: ```php $reflected = $method->getReturnType(); ... if ($reflected !== null && $reflected->allowsNull() && !str_contains($returnType, 'null')) { $returnType .= '|null'; } ``` `Utils::sanitizeDeclaration()` splits on `|` and already leaves `null` alone (it is in `Utils::$nativeTypes`), so no further change is needed. Do the same in `getParamType()` by reading `$refParam->getType()?->allowsNull()` instead of stripping `' or NULL'` out of the string export. Add `ReflectorTest` cases for `?Foo` and `?string`. ## Resolution formatReflectionType() appends '|null' when ReflectionType::allowsNull() says so, excluding mixed and null. '?X' and 'X|null' now document identically on both the return and the parameter side. ReflectorTest::testParams updated: it asserted the dropped null, which was the defect.
title: Nullable types lose their null: ?Foo renders as \Foo and ?string as string

body:
## Problem

Both documentation scripts redirect into the file they are supposed to produce or verify:

```json
"docs": "./bin/phpdoc-md generate src > docs.md",
"docs-check": "./bin/phpdoc-md generate src > docs.md && git diff --exit-code docs.md",
```

The shell truncates `docs.md` when it opens the redirect — before `bin/phpdoc-md` runs. Any failure
after that point (a class that cannot be reflected, a fatal error under a new PHP version, an
`InvalidArgumentException` from `execute()`, an interrupted run) leaves `docs.md` empty on disk.

`docs-check` compounds it: it is named as a read-only check and is wired into CI as one
("Check docs.md is up to date"), yet it overwrites the working copy before comparing, and compares
against the git index rather than against the file's prior contents.

## Evidence

```
$ wc -c < docs.md
22561
$ sh -c './bin/phpdoc-md generate NoSuchDirOrClass > docs.md'; echo "exit=$?"
exit=1
$ wc -c < docs.md
0
```

The file was destroyed by a command that never produced a single byte of output.

## Impact

A failed docs run silently deletes the committed API reference — the document the README links to
as the rendered example. On a developer machine the loss is recoverable from git, but the failure
mode is invisible: the exit code is the only signal, and anyone who runs `composer docs` and then
inspects an empty `docs.md` will read it as "the generator produced nothing" rather than "the
generator failed".

## Fix

Generate to a temporary file and move it into place only on success:

```json
"docs": "./bin/phpdoc-md generate src > docs.md.tmp && mv docs.md.tmp docs.md",
"docs-check": "./bin/phpdoc-md generate src > docs.md.tmp && diff -u docs.md docs.md.tmp && rm docs.md.tmp"
```

The `docs-check` form above is also a true check: it never writes `docs.md`, and it compares
against the file on disk rather than against the index, so it behaves identically on a dirty tree.
Add `docs.md.tmp` to `.gitignore`.

## Resolution
composer docs writes docs.md.tmp and moves it into place; docs-check writes the temp file, diffs against docs.md and removes it, never touching docs.md. Verified: a failing generate leaves docs.md byte-identical. docs.md.tmp added to .gitignore.
title: composer docs and docs-check truncate docs.md to zero bytes whenever generation fails
