## Problem `execute()` emits the finished markdown with `OutputInterface::writeln()` at its default verbosity: ```php $output->writeln('## Table of contents' . PHP_EOL); $output->writeln(implode(PHP_EOL, $tableOfContent)); ... $output->writeln(PHP_EOL . $docString); ``` Symfony's `OutputFormatter` parses the string for `` sequences. Text that happens to match a registered style name — `info`, `comment`, `error`, `question`, plus anything a custom `--tableGenerator` registers — is consumed: the tag is removed and, on a non-TTY, no replacement is emitted. The generator is a text-transformation tool whose entire output is data, not console chrome; it should be writing with `OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW`. ## Evidence ```php /** * Prints coloured and red output. */ class Formatting { /** * Returns an info map with a comment. */ public function mapped() { return []; } } ``` ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate ./Src -b bootstrap.php | cat -A | grep Prints > Prints coloured and red output.$ $ ... | grep mapped | public | mapped() : array
Returns an info map with a comment. | ``` Six tags in the source docblocks, zero in the output. The words survive; the markup around them is gone. ## Impact Any docblock that documents HTML, XML, or console-style markup loses it. The loss is silent and lossy in one direction only — a description explaining "wrap the value in `` to colour it" comes out as "wrap the value in to colour it", which is worse than mangled: it reads as correct prose while stating the opposite of the source. ## Fix Write every generated line raw: ```php $output->writeln('## Table of contents' . PHP_EOL, OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW); $output->writeln(implode(PHP_EOL, $tableOfContent), OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW); $output->writeln(PHP_EOL . $docString, OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW); ``` `OUTPUT_RAW` bypasses the formatter entirely and is exactly the intent here. Add a `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` fixture whose class docblock contains `x` and assert the tag survives into the output. ## Resolution All three writeln() calls now pass OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW. , and in docblocks survive into the markdown. Regression: PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testConsoleStyleTagsInDocblocksSurvive over test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/PlainClass.php.
title: Markdown is written through Symfony's output formatter, which deletes style tags from docblock text

body:
## Problem

`findClassInFile()` splits the file on the *host's* line separator, then trims the namespace with a
charlist that does not include carriage return:

```php
foreach (explode(PHP_EOL, file_get_contents($file)) as $line) {
    ...
    $ns = trim(current(array_slice(explode('namespace', $line), 1)), '; ');
```

On Linux `PHP_EOL` is `"\n"`, so a CRLF file yields lines ending in `\r`. `trim($str, '; ')` stops
at the `\r`, leaving the semicolon in place, and the resulting namespace is `\Probe;\r`.

## Evidence

A file written with CRLF endings declaring `Probe\CrLf`:

```
$ php -r '... $m->invoke($cmd, "Src/CrLf.php")'
array (
  0 => '\Probe;',      // trailing \r, semicolon not trimmed
  1 => '\Probe;\CrLf',
)
```

`class_exists('\Probe;'."\r".'\CrLf')` is false, so `findClassesInDir()` drops the file. The class
is absent from the generated document even though it was loaded and reflectable — the same run's
bootstrap had already `require_once`d it.

## Impact

A repository checked out on Windows, or one that has any CRLF file (mixed line endings survive
`git checkout` when `.gitattributes` does not normalise, and this repo's `.gitattributes` sets only
`export-ignore` rules), loses those classes from its documentation with no warning. The failure is
environment-dependent: the same source tree documents differently on different machines.

## Fix

Split on any line ending and trim whitespace as well as the statement punctuation:

```php
foreach (preg_split('/\R/', file_get_contents($file)) as $line) {
    ...
    $ns = trim(current(array_slice(explode('namespace', $line), 1)), "; \t\r\n");
```

`\R` matches `\n`, `\r\n` and `\r`. Add a CRLF fixture file under `test/Acme/Fixtures/` and assert
it appears in the generated output. `.gitattributes` should also gain `*.php text eol=lf` so the
fixture keeps its endings through a checkout.

## Resolution
Line-ending dependence removed with findClassInFile()'s tokeniser rewrite — the lexer handles CRLF, CR and LF alike. Regression: PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testClassInACrlfFileIsDiscovered over a real CRLF fixture, pinned by '.gitattributes' ('*.php text eol=lf' plus '-text' for that one file).
title: Files whose line endings are not PHP_EOL are silently skipped by the directory scanner

body:
## Problem

`findClassesInDir()` filters on nothing but "is a file":

```php
foreach ($entries as $f) {
    if ($f->isFile() && !$f->isLink()) {
        [$ns, $className] = $this->findClassInFile($f->getRealPath());
```

and `findClassInFile()` immediately does `file_get_contents($file)` followed by `explode()` into a
line array. Images, archives, SQLite files, minified bundles, fixtures — all are slurped into
memory in full and split into lines before being discarded.

## Evidence

One 80 MB binary blob dropped next to a single PHP fixture:

```
$ /usr/bin/time -f 'peak RSS: %M KB, wall %e s' ./bin/phpdoc-md generate ./big >/dev/null
peak RSS: 232260 KB, wall 0.45 s

$ rm ./big/blob.bin
$ /usr/bin/time -f 'peak RSS: %M KB, wall %e s' ./bin/phpdoc-md generate ./big >/dev/null
peak RSS: 55276 KB, wall 0.08 s
```

An 80 MB file costs ~177 MB of resident memory — the contents plus the exploded line array.

## Impact

Pointing the generator at a source tree that contains a large non-PHP asset exhausts
`memory_limit` and aborts the run. The default CLI `memory_limit` is often 128 MB, below the
figure measured above. Combined with the `composer docs` redirect defect, an out-of-memory abort
also leaves `docs.md` truncated.

## Fix

Skip non-PHP files before reading:

```php
if ($f->isFile() && !$f->isLink() && strtolower($f->getExtension()) === 'php') {
```

The README already requires "Each class must be defined in its own file with the file name being
the same as the class name", so restricting to `.php` narrows nothing that is documented as
supported. Reading line-by-line with `SplFileObject` instead of `file_get_contents()` would bound
the cost further, since the loop `break`s at the first declaration anyway.

## Resolution
findClassesInDir() now skips anything without a .php extension. Measured: the 80 MB blob that cost 232 MB peak RSS now costs 55 MB, the same as without it. README's Requirements section states the extension rule.
title: The directory scanner reads every file whole regardless of extension

body:
## Problem

README.md:92 documents the option as:

| `--ignore`, `-i` | none | Comma-separated directory **names** to skip, at any depth |

`shouldIgnoreDirectory()` compares with `str_ends_with()`:

```php
foreach ($ignores as $dir) {
    $dir = trim($dir);
    if (!empty($dir) && str_ends_with($dirName, $dir)) {
        return true;
    }
}
```

Any directory whose name *ends with* the given string is skipped, so `--ignore` silently matches
far more than the names it is given.

## Evidence

The repository's own fixture tree contains `Tree/Keep/`, `Tree/skipme/` and `Tree/Sub/skipme/`:

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate test/Acme/Fixtures/Tree | grep -c 'Skipped'
4
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate test/Acme/Fixtures/Tree --ignore=me | grep -c 'Skipped'
0
```

`--ignore=me` — a two-letter string matching no directory in the tree — removed both `skipme`
directories.

## Impact

`--ignore=test` also drops `latest/`, `manifest/`, `mytest/`. The user gets a document missing
classes they never asked to exclude, with no diagnostic. The narrower the ignore string, the more
it eats.

## Fix

Compare names, matching what the README already promises:

```php
if ($dir !== '' && $dirName === $dir) {
    return true;
}
```

If suffix or glob matching is actually wanted, `fnmatch($dir, $dirName)` gives it explicitly and
the README should then document patterns rather than names. `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` has
`testIgnoreAppliesToNestedDirectories` already; add an assertion that `--ignore=me` leaves
`skipme` in place.

## Resolution
shouldIgnoreDirectory() compares whole names instead of str_ends_with(). '--ignore=me' leaves both skipme fixtures in place; '--ignore=skipme' still removes them. Regression: PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testIgnoreMatchesWholeDirectoryNamesOnly. README documents the whole-name rule.
title: --ignore is a suffix match, not a directory-name match, contradicting the README

## Problem

No file under `src/` has `declare(strict_types=1)` — only `tools/check-php-support.php` does:

```
$ grep -rln strict_types src bin test tools
tools/check-php-support.php
```

The library relies on coercive mode in at least two places where a `bool` is returned or assigned
through a `string` contract:

`DocInfo` declares `string` returns over a default structure holding `false`:

```php
public static array $defaultStructure = ['return' => '', 'params' => [], 'description' => '',
                                         'example' => false, 'deprecated' => false, 'see' => []];
public function getExample(): string          { return $this->data['example']; }
public function getDeprecationMessage(): string { return $this->data['deprecated']; }
```

`PHPDocsMDCommand::execute()` assigns `false` to a `string` property:

```php
private string $methodRegex = '';
...
$this->methodRegex = $input->getOption(self::OPT_METHOD_REGEX) ?: false;
```

## Evidence

```
$ php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; $d = new PHPDocsMD\DocInfo();
          var_dump($d->getExample(), $d->getDeprecationMessage());'
string(0) ""
string(0) ""
```

`false` in, `""` out. Under `declare(strict_types=1)` each of these sites raises a `TypeError`
instead. Psalm does not catch them because `DocInfo::$data` is an untyped `array`, and psalm runs
at `errorLevel="5"` — it reports "69 other issues found" at info level today.

## Impact

The coercion is load-bearing: adding `declare(strict_types=1)` to these files today produces fatal
errors at runtime rather than a clean no-op. That makes the codebase resistant to being tightened,
and it hides the real design issue — that `DocInfo`'s data structure uses `false` as "absent" while
its accessors promise `string`.

## Fix

Fix the sentinels first, then add the declaration:

```php
public static array $defaultStructure = ['return' => '', 'params' => [], 'description' => '',
                                         'example' => '', 'deprecated' => '', 'see' => []];
```

Both consumers already treat the value as a string (`if ($docInfo->getDeprecationMessage())`,
`if ($example = $class->getExample())`), so `''` is behaviour-preserving. Then:

```php
$this->methodRegex = (string)$input->getOption(self::OPT_METHOD_REGEX);
```

and add `declare(strict_types=1);` to every file in `src/`, `bin/` and `test/`. Run the suite after
each file to catch remaining coercion sites; the existing 74 tests are the regression net.

## Resolution
declare(strict_types=1) added to all 15 src files, bin/phpdoc-md and all test files. Sentinels fixed first: DocInfo::$defaultStructure now holds '' for example/deprecated, and methodRegex is cast rather than assigned false. Two latent coercions surfaced and were fixed: getDocComment() returning false into str_replace(), and strrpos() returning false into substr() in stripAwayNamespace(). Psalm inference rose from 92.8% to 94.2%.
title: src/ declares no strict_types, and several return values depend on silent bool-to-string coercion

## Problem

`.github/workflows/php.yml` — the workflow that runs on every push to `main` and every pull
request — has no `permissions:` key at workflow or job level. It therefore receives whatever the
repository or organisation default is, which for repositories created before the default changed
is read/write on `contents`, `packages`, `issues`, `pull-requests` and more.

The repository's other two workflows do scope their tokens:

```yaml
# composer-diff.yml
permissions:
  pull-requests: write

# semantic-commits.yml
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
```

so the omission is inconsistent with the project's own established practice, not merely with a
general guideline.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -c permissions .github/workflows/php.yml
0
$ grep -n permissions .github/workflows/composer-diff.yml .github/workflows/semantic-commits.yml
composer-diff.yml:6:permissions:
semantic-commits.yml:12:    permissions:
```

`php.yml` runs `composer install`, `composer update` and `composer audit`, all of which execute
third-party code (Composer plugins, package scripts) with that token present in the runner
environment.

## Impact

A compromised or malicious dependency executing during `composer install` on the `push` trigger —
where the token is not downgraded to read-only as it is for fork pull requests — can use
`GITHUB_TOKEN` to push commits, publish packages, or edit issues. Nothing in this workflow needs
write access to anything.

## Fix

Add a top-level block; `contents: read` is all any step here requires (checkout, install, test,
lint, and the Codecov upload, which authenticates with `CODECOV_TOKEN` rather than
`GITHUB_TOKEN`):

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
```

## Resolution
php.yml now declares 'permissions: contents: read' at workflow level, matching the scoping the other two workflows already had.
title: php.yml declares no permissions block, unlike the repository's two other workflows

## Problem

`ReflectorInterface` declares a single method and is implemented by exactly one class. No code
anywhere — `src/`, `test/`, `bin/` — type-hints, accepts, returns, or otherwise references the
interface.

```
$ grep -rn "ReflectorInterface" src test bin
src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/ReflectorInterface.php:12:interface ReflectorInterface
src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php:28:class Reflector implements ReflectorInterface
```

The two call sites that construct a reflector both name the concrete class and immediately call
methods that are *not* on the interface, so the abstraction cannot be substituted at either:

```php
// PHPDocsMDCommand::getClassEntity()
$reflector = new Reflector($name);
$reflector->setVisibilityFilter($this->visibilityFilter);   // not on ReflectorInterface
$reflector->setMethodRegex($this->methodRegex);             // not on ReflectorInterface

// FunctionFinder::loadClassEntity()
$reflector = new Reflector($className, $this);
```

Contrast `TableGenerator`, the neighbouring interface: it is a genuine extension point, named by
the `--tableGenerator` option, type-checked in `buildTableGenerator()`, and exercised by
`SpyTableGenerator` in the test suite.

## Evidence

The grep above is exhaustive over the first-party tree. The interface also has no `@api` marker,
is not mentioned in README.md, and appears in `docs.md` only because the generator documents
everything in `src/`.

## Impact

It is dead flexibility: a public type that constrains nothing, costs a file and a `docs.md`
section, and misleads readers into thinking the reflector is pluggable when neither call site can
accept a substitute. Removing it costs nothing; keeping it means either the interface or both call
sites are wrong.

## Fix

Either delete it —

```
rm src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/ReflectorInterface.php
# drop "implements ReflectorInterface" from Reflector
```

— or make it real: move `setVisibilityFilter()` and `setMethodRegex()` onto the interface and have
`PHPDocsMDCommand::getClassEntity()` and `FunctionFinder::loadClassEntity()` depend on
`ReflectorInterface` through an injected factory. Deletion is the smaller change and matches the
current design, in which the reflector is not an extension point. Regenerate `docs.md` afterwards.

## Resolution
ReflectorInterface deleted and 'implements' dropped from Reflector, along with the now-redundant #[\Override] on getClassEntity(). BREAKING: removes a public type; needs a major version bump.
title: ReflectorInterface has one implementation and no consumers

## Problem

`888bfa5` is typed as a breaking change:

```
chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout action (v4.4.0 → v7.0.1) (#11)

Signed-off-by: renovate[bot] <...>
Co-authored-by: renovate[bot] <...>
```

The `!` marker is Conventional Commits' declaration of a breaking change, and the specification
requires it to be accompanied by a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer describing the break. There is no
such footer.

More importantly the commit does not break anything for a consumer of this package. Its entire
diff is two workflow files:

```
$ git show --name-only --format= 888bfa5
.github/workflows/composer-diff.yml
.github/workflows/php.yml
```

Both are `export-ignore`d in `.gitattributes`, so they never reach a consumer's `vendor/`
directory at all.

## Evidence

The commit above, plus `.gitattributes`:

```
/.github            export-ignore
```

and `semantic-commits.yml`, which lints PR titles against the Conventional Commits grammar. That
linter validates *shape*, not truthfulness, so `chore(deps)!` passes.

## Impact

The repository already enforces conventional commits, which is the precondition for automated
versioning. The moment a release workflow is added (release-please, semantic-release, or a manual
`git log`-driven changelog), a `!` on a GitHub Actions bump cuts a major version for a change no
consumer can observe, and the changelog's "Breaking Changes" section lists an entry with no
description because no footer exists. Renovate will keep emitting these on every action major bump.

## Fix

Constrain the manager in `renovate.json` so CI-only updates are never typed as breaking, and are
scoped away from the package's own semantics:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["local>ivuorinen/renovate-config"],
  "packageRules": [
    {
      "matchManagers": ["github-actions"],
      "semanticCommitType": "ci",
      "semanticCommitScope": "actions",
      "commitMessageSuffix": ""
    }
  ]
}
```

`matchManagers: ["github-actions"]` is exact, so nothing about Composer updates changes. Verify by
checking that the next Renovate action PR is titled `ci(actions): ...` with no `!`.

## Resolution
renovate.json gained a packageRules entry scoping github-actions updates to semanticCommitType 'ci', scope 'actions', with an empty commitMessageSuffix so no '!' is emitted. Composer updates are untouched.
title: A CI-only action bump is recorded as a breaking change with no BREAKING CHANGE footer

## Problem

This is the residue of `audit-9fc57d49`. Two of that finding's recommendations were tried and
reverted, because they are wrong for this repository's shape rather than merely inconvenient:

**`test/` cannot join phpcs.** Adding `<file>test</file>` to phpcs.xml produces 11 PSR-2 errors
that cannot be fixed without breaking the fixtures:

```
test/ReflectorTest.php:9      Each class must be in a namespace of at least one level
test/UseInspectorTest.php:5   Each class must be in a namespace of at least one level
test/MDTableGeneratorTest.php Each class must be in a namespace of at least one level
test/Acme/ExampleClass.php    Each class must be in a file by itself  (x9)
```

`test/Acme/ExampleClass.php` declares nine classes in one file *on purpose* — that multi-class,
multi-interface layout is precisely what `ReflectorTest` reflects over. Splitting it changes what
is under test. The unnamespaced test classes are a deliberate PHPUnit convention here.

**`findUnusedCode="true"` cannot be enabled.** Turning it on raised 7 `PossiblyUnusedMethod` and
1 `UnusedClass` against `src` alone. For a library, every public API method is unreferenced from
inside the package by definition, so the check reports the package's own surface as dead. It also
fired `UnusedClass` on every PHPUnit test class when `test/` was in scope. It was reset to `false`.

## Evidence

```
$ vendor/bin/phpcs           # with test/ added
FOUND 9 ERRORS AFFECTING 9 LINES   (test/Acme/ExampleClass.php)
FOUND 1 ERROR  AFFECTING 1 LINE    (test/ReflectorTest.php)
FOUND 1 ERROR  AFFECTING 1 LINE    (test/UseInspectorTest.php)

$ vendor/bin/psalm           # findUnusedCode="true", src only
15 MissingOverrideAttribute / 7 PossiblyUnusedMethod / 2 PossiblyUnusedReturnValue
 1 UnusedVariable / 1 UnusedClass ...
31 errors found
```

Current committed state: `phpcs.xml` covers `src` + `bin` and passes clean; `psalm.xml` covers
`src` with `findUnusedCode="false"` and reports `No errors found!`. Both gate CI.

## Impact

595 lines of test code and the fixtures receive no style or static checking. A type error in a
test is caught only when that test runs, and never by the linters.

## Fix

Neither gap is fixable by a config toggle; each needs a decision:

1. **Namespace the test classes** (`namespace PHPDocsMD\Tests;`) and add
   `"PHPDocsMD\\Tests\\": "test/"` to `autoload-dev`. That clears the three namespace errors and
   lets `test/*Test.php` join phpcs — while still excluding `test/Acme/` via
   `<exclude-pattern>test/Acme/*</exclude-pattern>`, since the fixture's one-class-per-file
   violation is intentional and permanent.
2. **Leave `findUnusedCode` off.** Psalm's unused-code detection is not meaningful for a library's
   public surface. If dead private members are the actual concern, the narrower
   `UnusedPrivateMethod`/`UnusedPrivateProperty` issue handlers can be enabled individually
   instead:
   ```xml
   <issueHandlers>
       <UnusedPrivateMethod errorLevel="error" />
       <UnusedPrivateProperty errorLevel="error" />
   </issueHandlers>
   ```
   That would have caught `Utils::getSanitizedTypeDeclaration()` without reporting the package's
   own API as dead.

## Resolution
Option 1 from the finding applied. Test classes namespaced PHPDocsMD\Tests with 'PHPDocsMD\\Tests\\': 'test/' in autoload-dev; SpyTableGenerator extracted to its own file to satisfy one-class-per-file. phpcs.xml now covers test/ with test/Acme/* excluded, because ExampleClass.php's nine-classes-in-one-file layout is what ReflectorTest reflects over and CrLfClass.php must keep CRLF. phpcs passes over 23 files. findUnusedCode stays false per the finding's option 2.
title: test/ is excluded from linting and static analysis, and cannot be included as it stands

## Problem

`findClassesInDir()` calls `class_exists($className, true)` (PHPDocsMDCommand.php:321)
to decide whether a discovered type is documentable. With autoloading enabled that
call *executes* the class file. If the file loads but its parent class or an
implemented interface is absent — an optional/suggested dependency the consumer did
not install — PHP raises an `Error` that unwinds all the way to `bin/phpdoc-md` and
kills the run.

There is no per-class recovery: one unloadable class discards documentation for every
other class in the tree.

## Evidence

`vendor/symfony/console` is an ordinary, fully installed package in this very repo.
Documenting it is impossible:

```
$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate vendor/symfony/console
phpdoc-md: Class "Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\DataCollector\DataCollector" not found
$ echo $?
2
```

Output written: 0 bytes, 0 classes — out of 132 source files.

Working around it one directory at a time only surfaces the next one:

```
$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --ignore=DataCollector vendor/symfony/console
phpdoc-md: Class "Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request" not found

$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --ignore=DataCollector,Messenger,Debug vendor/symfony/console
phpdoc-md: Interface "Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Compiler\CompilerPassInterface" not found
```

The stack trace confirms the origin is the autoload triggered by `class_exists()`:

```
Error: Class "Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\DataCollector\DataCollector" not found
#0 vendor/composer/ClassLoader.php(576): include()
#3 class_exists()
```

## Impact

Any project that ships a class with an optional integration point — a Symfony
compiler pass, a PSR-11 bridge, a framework-specific subclass, a class guarded by an
optional PHP extension — cannot be documented at all. The user gets a one-line
message naming a class they never asked about, no partial document, and no
indication that the other 130 classes were fine. `composer docs`-style pipelines
(`phpdoc-md generate src > api.md`) truncate the committed API reference to empty on
the failing run, because the redirect has already opened the file.

## Fix

Isolate the per-class load so one failure skips one class. In `findClassesInDir()`
replace the inline `class_exists(...) || interface_exists(...) || trait_exists(...)`
test with:

```php
if ($className && $this->isDocumentable($className)) {
    $collection[$ns][] = $className;
}
```

```php
private function isDocumentable(string $className): bool
{
    try {
        return class_exists($className, true)
            || interface_exists($className)
            || trait_exists($className);
    } catch (\Throwable $e) {
        // A class whose parent or interface is not installed cannot be
        // reflected. Skip it rather than discarding the whole tree.
        fwrite(STDERR, sprintf(
            'phpdoc-md: skipping %s (%s)%s',
            $className,
            $e->getMessage(),
            PHP_EOL
        ));

        return false;
    }
}
```

Apply the same guard around `getClassEntity()` in the render loop, since
`new ReflectionClass()` fails the same way for a class reached through the
comma-separated argument form.

Add a fixture class extending a non-existent parent and assert that a directory
containing it still documents its siblings and still exits 0.

## Resolution
isDocumentable() catches the autoload Throwable and skips the one class with a stderr note; symfony/console now yields 129 classes, exit 0, 3 skipped. Test: testAnUnloadableClassDoesNotAbortTheRun + Fixtures/Broken.
title: Directory scan aborts entirely when one class has an unsatisfied optional dependency

## Problem

`DocInfoExtractor::extractInfoFromComment()` keeps two structured, array-valued keys
in `$tags`: `params` and `see`. The generic "start new tag" branch
(DocInfoExtractor.php:76-86) does not reserve them:

```php
$current_tag = substr($words[0], 1);
array_splice($words, 0, 1);
if (empty($tags[$current_tag])) {
    $tags[$current_tag] = '';          // <- overwrites the array with a string
}

/** @psalm-suppress PossiblyInvalidOperand */
$tags[$current_tag] .= trim(implode(' ', $words));
```

A tag named `@params` sets `$current_tag = 'params'`. `$tags['params']` is `[]`, which
is `empty()`, so it is replaced by `''`. A later real `@param` line then executes
`$tags['params'][$name] = $data` (line 69) against a string, with a non-numeric
offset — a fatal `Error` in PHP 8.

The two `@psalm-suppress` annotations on lines 84 and 93 are what keep static analysis
from reporting this.

## Evidence

```php
<?php
namespace Probe;
class ParamsTypo
{
    /**
     * @params string $a
     * @param string $a the real one
     */
    public function boom(string $a): void {}
}
```

```
$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\ParamsTypo'
phpdoc-md: Cannot access offset of type string on string
$ echo $?
2
```

No document is produced.

## Impact

`@params` is a common typo for `@param`, and the crash message names neither the file,
the class, nor the tag — it is untraceable from the output alone. One mistyped tag
anywhere in a source tree takes the whole documentation build down, and in a
`generate src > api.md` pipeline it leaves the API reference empty.

The same collision exists for any future array-valued key added to
`DocInfo::$defaultStructure`.

## Fix

Reserve the structured keys in the generic branch, and drop the suppressions that
were hiding the type confusion:

```php
private const STRUCTURED_TAGS = ['params', 'see'];

// ... in the else branch:
$current_tag = substr($words[0], 1);
if (in_array($current_tag, self::STRUCTURED_TAGS, true)) {
    // A free-form tag must not clobber a structured collection.
    $current_tag = 'description';
    continue;
}
```

Then remove `/** @psalm-suppress PossiblyInvalidOperand */` (line 84) and
`/** @psalm-suppress InvalidArrayOffset */` (line 93) and confirm psalm is clean —
`findUnusedPsalmSuppress="true"` is already set in psalm.xml, so a leftover
suppression will be reported.

Add a test asserting that a docblock containing both `@params` and `@param` produces
the documented parameter and does not throw.

## Resolution
STRUCTURED_TAGS reserves 'params' so a free-form tag cannot replace the array; both psalm-suppress annotations removed and psalm stays clean. Test: testATagCollidingWithAStructuredKeyDoesNotCrash.
title: A docblock tag colliding with a structured key (@params) crashes the run

## Problem

`Reflector::getClassFunctions()` applies `--methodRegex` with an unchecked
`preg_match()` (Reflector.php:110-118):

```php
$methodReflections = array_filter(
    $methodReflections,
    fn (ReflectionMethod $reflectionMethod) => preg_match(
        $this->methodRegex,
        $reflectionMethod->name
    )
);
```

`preg_match()` returns `false` — not a raised exception — when the pattern is
malformed. `array_filter` treats `false` as "exclude", so *every* method is dropped
from *every* class. The command then completes normally and returns
`self::SUCCESS` (0).

`setMethodRegex()` (Reflector.php:519) accepts any string without validating it, and
`PHPDocsMDCommand::execute()` passes the raw option value straight through.

## Evidence

`get` is a plausible thing for a user to type — the README's own example uses
`--methodRegex='/^get/'`, and the delimiters are easy to omit:

```
$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --methodRegex='get' src
## Table of contents

- [\PHPDocsMD\DocInfo](#class-phpdocsmddocinfo)
- [\PHPDocsMD\DocInfoExtractor](#class-phpdocsmddocinfoextractor)
...
```

Method rows emitted: **0**. Exit code: **0**.

Stderr carries only `PHP Warning: preg_match(): Delimiter must not be alphanumeric,
backslash, or NUL byte`, which is invisible under the default `display_errors=Off`
of most production and CI php.ini files.

## Impact

A full table of contents and a per-class heading for every class, with every function
table empty — output that reads as "this project has no public API" rather than as an
error. Because the exit code is 0, `composer docs`
(`phpdoc-md generate src > docs.md.tmp && mv docs.md.tmp docs.md`) commits the
gutted document, and `composer docs-check` in CI then fails on the *next* run for a
reason unrelated to the actual cause.

## Fix

Validate once, at the point the pattern is accepted, and fail loudly.
`Reflector::setMethodRegex()`:

```php
public function setMethodRegex(string $methodRegex): self
{
    // preg_match() returns false rather than throwing on a bad pattern, and
    // array_filter() reads that as "exclude" — every method would silently vanish.
    if ($methodRegex !== '' && @preg_match($methodRegex, '') === false) {
        throw new InvalidArgumentException(
            sprintf('Invalid --methodRegex "%s": %s', $methodRegex, preg_last_error_msg())
        );
    }

    $this->methodRegex = $methodRegex;

    return $this;
}
```

`InvalidArgumentException` is already imported in Reflector.php and is already the
class used for the unknown-visibility rejection, so this matches the existing
convention and surfaces through Symfony with a non-zero exit.

Extend `ReflectorTest::regexFiltersAndExpectedMethods` with an invalid-pattern case
asserting the exception, mirroring `testUnknownVisibilityFilterIsRejected`.

## Resolution
setMethodRegex() validates the pattern and throws InvalidArgumentException; exit is now 1 with a message instead of 0 with an empty document. Test: testInvalidMethodRegexIsRejected.
title: Invalid --methodRegex silently emits an empty document with exit code 0

## Problem `ClassEntity::generateAnchor()` (ClassEntity.php:122-133) builds the anchor by *deleting* the namespace separator rather than replacing it: ```php return strtolower( str_replace( [':', ' ', '\\', '(', ')'], ['', '-', '', '', ''], $title ) ); ``` Two distinct fully-qualified names that differ only in where a namespace boundary falls therefore collapse onto the same anchor. `A\FooBar` and `A\Foo\Bar` both become `class-afoobar`. Every consumer of the anchor is affected: the table-of-contents entry (PHPDocsMDCommand.php:165-169), the emitted `` (line 204), and the `$classLinks` map used for cross-reference substitution (line 171). ## Evidence Two classes, `\Probe\Anchors\FooBar` and `\Probe\Anchors\Foo\Bar`: ``` $ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php probe/anchors - [\Probe\Anchors\FooBar](#class-probeanchorsfoobar) - [\Probe\Anchors\Foo\Bar](#class-probeanchorsfoobar)
``` Both TOC entries link to `#class-probeanchorsfoobar`, and two elements share that id. Every renderer resolves a duplicate id to the first occurrence, so the link for `Foo\Bar` navigates to `FooBar`'s section — silently, with no broken-link indication. ## Impact Wrong navigation in the generated document, and wrong cross-reference links wherever either class appears as a parameter or return type. The failure is invisible: the markdown is well-formed and the links resolve, just to the wrong section. Namespace layouts that produce this (`Acme\Repository\User` alongside `Acme\RepositoryUser`, `App\Http\Client` alongside `App\HttpClient`) are ordinary. ## Fix Replace the separator with the hyphen already used for spaces, so the boundary survives: ```php return strtolower( str_replace( [':', ' ', '\\', '(', ')'], ['', '-', '-', '', ''], $title ) ); ``` `\Probe\Anchors\FooBar` then yields `class--probe-anchors-foobar` and `\Probe\Anchors\Foo\Bar` yields `class--probe-anchors-foo-bar` — distinct, and still valid GitHub-flavoured markdown anchors since the `` is emitted explicitly rather than inferred from the heading. This changes every anchor in a generated document, so `docs.md` must be regenerated (`composer docs`) in the same commit or `composer docs-check` will fail CI. `ReflectorTest::testClass` asserts `class-acmeexampleclass-abstract` and must be updated to the new form. Add a case asserting that `A\FooBar` and `A\Foo\Bar` produce different anchors. ## Resolution generateAnchor() maps the namespace separator to '-' and collapses hyphen runs. docs.md regenerated; ReflectorTest and PHPDocsMDCommandTest anchor assertions updated. Test: testAnchorsDistinguishNamespaceBoundaries.
title: Anchor generation collapses distinct class names onto one anchor

## Problem

`DocInfoExtractor::extractInfoFromComment()` treats a line as opening a new tag when
its first word *contains* `@` anywhere (DocInfoExtractor.php:61):

```php
if (!str_contains($words[0], '@')) {
```

An ordinary prose line whose first word is an e-mail address matches. The line, and
every line after it up to the next real tag, is diverted into a junk tag keyed on the
remainder of the address (`substr('maintainer@example.com', 1)` →
`'aintainer@example.com'`), which nothing ever reads.

## Evidence

```php
/**
 * Contact the maintainer.
 * maintainer@example.com is the address to use.
 * This trailing sentence must survive.
 */
class AtWord { public function braced(): void {} }
```

Generated output:

```
### Class: \Probe\AtWord

> Contact the maintainer.
```

The e-mail line and the sentence that follows it are absent from the document
entirely — not escaped, not garbled, silently dropped.

## Impact

Any class or method whose docblock mentions a contact address, a Twitter/GitHub
handle (`@ivuorinen maintains this`), or a package name containing `@` loses that
line *and the whole remainder of its description*. The output is well-formed markdown
with a truncated description, so there is nothing to notice at review time.

## Fix

Match the tag word by shape instead of by substring. In `extractInfoFromComment()`:

```php
// A tag is the first word, optionally wrapped in the inline braces
// phpDocumentor uses: "@param", "{@inheritDoc}". A word that merely
// contains "@" (an e-mail address) is prose, not a tag.
$isTag = preg_match('/^\{?@([A-Za-z][\w-]*)\}?$/', $words[0], $tagMatch) === 1;

if (!$isTag) {
    $joinWith = $current_tag === 'example' ? PHP_EOL : ' ';
    $tags[$current_tag] .= $joinWith . $line;
} elseif ($tagMatch[1] === 'param') {
    ...
}
```

This is the same edit that fixes the unrecognised `{@inheritDoc}` defect filed
separately; both symptoms come from this one test.

Add a fixture whose description contains an e-mail address and assert the full
description, including the text after that line, reaches `ClassEntity::getDescription()`.

## Resolution
Same regex change: a word merely containing '@' is prose again. Test: testAnEmailInADescriptionDoesNotTruncateIt.
title: A prose word containing @ is parsed as a tag and truncates the description

## Problem

`formatExampleComment()` is part of the `TableGenerator` contract
(TableGenerator.php:20) — a custom generator selected with `--tableGenerator` is
required to implement it, and `buildTableGenerator()` rejects any class that does not
implement the interface.

But for class-level `@example` blocks, `PHPDocsMDCommand::execute()` hardcodes the
built-in implementation (PHPDocsMDCommand.php:226-230):

```php
$line = sprintf(
    '###### Example%s%s',
    PHP_EOL,
    MDTableGenerator::formatExampleComment($example)   // <- not $tableGenerator
);
```

The `$tableGenerator` built two lines earlier is used for every other rendering
decision on the same class. Function-level examples do go through the selected
generator, because `MDTableGenerator::getTable()` calls `self::formatExampleComment()`
internally — so the same document mixes two formatters.

## Evidence

`test/SpyTableGenerator.php` implements `formatExampleComment()` as the identity
function:

```php
public static function formatExampleComment(string $example): string
{
    return $example;
}
```

Running with that generator selected, on a class carrying a class-level `@example`:

```
$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --tableGenerator='PHPDocsMD\Tests\SpyTableGenerator' 'Probe\Ex\WithExample'

### Class: \Probe\Ex\WithExample

> A class with a class-level example.

###### Example
```php
<?php
  $x = 1;
```
```

The ` ```php ` fence can only come from `MDTableGenerator::formatExampleComment()`.
The selected generator's identity implementation would have emitted the raw comment.

## Impact

`--tableGenerator` does not fully replace the renderer. A generator written for a
non-markdown target (HTML, reStructuredText, a docs-site format) still gets
markdown code fences injected into its class-level example blocks, corrupting the
output it produces. The interface promises control the command does not hand over.

## Fix

Call the selected generator:

```php
$line = sprintf(
    '###### Example%s%s',
    PHP_EOL,
    $tableGenerator::formatExampleComment($example)
);
```

`$tableGenerator` is typed as `TableGenerator`, which declares the static method, so
the call is type-safe and the `use PHPDocsMD\MDTableGenerator;` import can then be
dropped from PHPDocsMDCommand.php if nothing else needs it (it is still referenced in
`buildTableGenerator()`'s `$map`, so keep it).

Extend `PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testSeeFlagReachesTheTableGenerator`'s pattern: give
`SpyTableGenerator` a recorded `formatExampleComment` and assert the command routes a
class-level example through it.

## Resolution
Calls the selected generator statically instead of MDTableGenerator. Test: testClassLevelExamplesGoThroughTheSelectedGenerator.
title: --tableGenerator is ignored when formatting class-level examples

## Problem

The suite is 86 tests / 253 assertions and green, but every failure path this audit
demonstrated is untested. The three defects filed at High severity all live in code
that has tests exercising only its success cases:

1. **Invalid `--methodRegex`** — `ReflectorTest::regexFiltersAndExpectedMethods`
   (ReflectorTest.php:358-368) supplies three well-formed patterns and nothing else.
   There is no counterpart to `testUnknownVisibilityFilterIsRejected`, which does
   cover the analogous rejection path for `--visibility`.
2. **A class that cannot be autoloaded** — no fixture extends a missing parent, so
   nothing covers `findClassesInDir()`'s behaviour when `class_exists()` throws.
3. **A docblock tag colliding with a structured key** (`@params`) — no fixture
   contains a malformed or unknown tag at all.

Separately, `ReflectorTest::testFunctions:93` asserts absence with a falsy test:

```php
$this->assertTrue(empty($functions[7])); // Should be skipped since tagged with @ignore
```

`empty()` is satisfied by `null`, `0`, `''` and `false` alike, so this passes whether
the element is missing or merely falsy — and it does not pin the list length, so an
extra function appended at index 8 would go unnoticed.

## Evidence

```
$ vendor/bin/phpunit
OK (86 tests, 253 assertions)
```

Yet all three of these hold against the same tree:

```
$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --methodRegex='get' src | grep -c '^| public'
0                                    # exit code 0

$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate vendor/symfony/console
phpdoc-md: Class "Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\DataCollector\DataCollector" not found

$ php bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\ParamsTypo'
phpdoc-md: Cannot access offset of type string on string
```

A green suite is currently compatible with the tool producing an empty document, or
no document at all, on ordinary input.

## Impact

The suite gates the happy path only. Every regression in argument validation, in
autoload resilience, or in docblock-tag handling ships undetected — and `composer
docs-check` in CI cannot catch them either, because it runs the generator against
`src/`, which contains none of these shapes.

## Fix

Add the cases alongside the fixes for the findings they cover:

- `ReflectorTest`: an invalid-pattern row asserting `InvalidArgumentException`,
  mirroring `testUnknownVisibilityFilterIsRejected`.
- `test/Acme/Fixtures/Broken/UnloadableChild.php` extending a non-existent parent,
  plus a `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` case asserting its sibling classes still appear and
  the command still returns 0.
- A fixture with `@params` followed by `@param`, asserting the documented parameter
  is produced and nothing throws.

Tighten the `@ignore` assertion to pin the shape rather than falsiness:

```php
$this->assertCount(7, $functions, 'the @ignore-tagged function must not be included');
```

## Resolution
8 regression tests added (94 tests / 270 assertions, was 86 / 253) covering invalid regex, unloadable class, tag collision, braced inheritDoc, email-in-description, anchor collision, generator delegation, --no-examples. empty() assertion replaced with assertCount(7).

## Problem

`appendExamplesToEndOfTable(bool $toggle)` is declared on the public `TableGenerator`
interface (TableGenerator.php:27), implemented in `MDTableGenerator`
(MDTableGenerator.php:40), stubbed in `SpyTableGenerator`, and unit-tested by
`MDTableGeneratorTest::testAppendingExamplesCanBeDisabled`. Nothing in the shipped
program ever calls it.

```
$ grep -rn "appendExamplesToEndOfTable" src test bin tools
src/PHPDocsMD/TableGenerator.php:27:    public function appendExamplesToEndOfTable(bool $toggle): void;
src/PHPDocsMD/MDTableGenerator.php:40:    public function appendExamplesToEndOfTable(bool $toggle): void
test/MDTableGeneratorTest.php:168:        $tbl->appendExamplesToEndOfTable(false);
test/SpyTableGenerator.php:22:    public function appendExamplesToEndOfTable(bool $toggle): void
```

`PHPDocsMDCommand::execute()` calls `openTable()`, `doDeclareAbstraction()`,
`addFunc()` and `getTable()` on the generator — never this one. There is no CLI
option that reaches it, and the README's option table (README.md:90-98) does not list
one.

The behaviour it toggles is therefore permanently on for every user of the tool.

## Evidence

The grep above is exhaustive over first-party code. The only caller is the test that
exists to cover the method itself — a method whose sole consumer is its own test is
not wired into anything.

The nearest sibling toggle, `doDeclareAbstraction()`, *is* called by the command
(PHPDocsMDCommand.php:175), which is what makes the asymmetry a defect rather than a
design choice: the two were clearly meant to be a pair.

Note also that `openTable()` resets `declareAbstraction` to `true`
(MDTableGenerator.php:53) but does not reset `appendExamples`, so the two toggles do
not even share a lifecycle — further evidence that one was never exercised through
the command's call sequence.

## Impact

Dead flexibility carried on a published interface. Every third-party
`TableGenerator` implementation is obliged to implement a method the program will
never call, and a reader of the interface reasonably concludes the option is
reachable when it is not.

## Fix

Pick one, and say which in the commit:

**Wire it** — add the option, matching the existing `--see` / `--no-internal` shape:

```php
->addOption(
    self::OPT_NO_EXAMPLES,
    null,
    InputOption::VALUE_NONE,
    'Do not append @example blocks after each function table'
);
```

```php
$tableGenerator->openTable();
$tableGenerator->appendExamplesToEndOfTable(!$input->getOption(self::OPT_NO_EXAMPLES));
$tableGenerator->doDeclareAbstraction(!$class->isInterface());
```

and document it in README.md's option table. Note the ordering: `openTable()` must
come first, since it resets `declareAbstraction`.

**Or remove it** — drop the method from `TableGenerator`, `MDTableGenerator`,
`SpyTableGenerator` and `testAppendingExamplesCanBeDisabled`, and make
`$appendExamples` a constant `true`. This is a breaking change to a published
interface and needs a major version bump.

Wiring it is the smaller diff and preserves the interface; removing it is the
smaller codebase.

## Resolution
Wired rather than removed, to avoid a breaking interface change: new --no-examples option, set after openTable() since that resets declareAbstraction. README option table updated. Test: testExampleBlocksCanBeSuppressed.
title: appendExamplesToEndOfTable is on the public interface but unreachable from the CLI

## Problem

`LICENSE` carries a single copyright line naming only the original upstream author
and a decade-old year range:

```
Copyright (c) 2015-2016 Victor Jonsson
```

`composer.json` declares three authors — Victor Jonsson, Grav CMS and Ismo Vuorinen —
and the package is published as `ivuorinen/markdowndocs` with `"license": "MIT"`.
The fork has since been substantially rewritten (the current `src/` bears little
resemblance to the 2016 tree: `declare(strict_types=1)` throughout, PHP 8.2+ typed
properties, a token-based `UseInspector` and `findClassInFile`, `Composer\InstalledVersions`
version resolution). None of that work is covered by any copyright notice.

## Evidence

```
$ head -1 LICENSE
Copyright (c) 2015-2016 Victor Jonsson

$ grep -A12 '"authors"' composer.json
        {"name": "Victor Jonsson",  ...},
        {"name": "Grav CMS",        ...},
        {"name": "Ismo Vuorinen",   ...}
```

`.gitattributes` ships `LICENSE` to consumers (it is explicitly listed under
"Do NOT export-ignore"), so this is the notice every downstream user receives.

## Impact

MIT requires the copyright notice to be retained in redistributions. Retaining the
upstream notice is correct and must stay; the gap is that the fork's own
contributions carry no notice at all, so downstream users have no record of who holds
copyright in the code they actually received, and the stated year range is wrong for
the work as shipped. Grav CMS is credited as an author in `composer.json` but appears
in no notice.

This is a compliance/attribution gap, not a licensing conflict: MIT → MIT is
compatible, `symfony/console` is MIT, and `composer audit` / `osv-scanner` /
`trivy fs` report no dependency-licence problems.

## Fix

Add the fork's copyright alongside the original, preserving upstream attribution:

```
Copyright (c) 2015-2016 Victor Jonsson
Copyright (c) 2016-2020 Grav CMS <hello@getgrav.org>
Copyright (c) 2020-2026 Ismo Vuorinen

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, ...
```

Confirm the Grav CMS year range against the git history of the fork point before
committing it; if that provenance is not established, drop that line and keep the
other two.

## Resolution
Added Grav CMS (2017-2021) and Ismo Vuorinen (2022-2026) copyright lines, year ranges taken from git log per author. Upstream's own 2015-2016 line left verbatim rather than rewritten.
title: LICENSE copyright covers only the 2015-2016 upstream author

## Problem

`.github/workflows/composer-diff.yml` grants `pull-requests: write` and posts a
comment, but is triggered by `pull_request`:

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'composer.lock'
permissions:
  pull-requests: write
```

For a pull request opened from a fork, GitHub issues a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`
regardless of the `permissions:` block — the block can only *reduce* the token's
scope, never raise it above what the trigger allows. The
`marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` step therefore receives HTTP 403 and fails.

## Evidence

The workflow's own `permissions` block requests write; GitHub's documented behaviour
for `pull_request` from a forked repository is that the token is read-only for all
scopes. The comment step has no `continue-on-error` and no `if` guard on the event's
origin, so the failure is terminal for the job:

```yaml
      - uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@...
        if: ${{ steps.composer_diff.outputs.composer_diff_exit_code != 0 }}
```

The only guard present is on whether the diff is empty, not on whether the token can
write.

The repository is public and carries a `CODEOWNERS` file and a
semantic-PR-title check — it is set up to accept outside contributions, which is
exactly the case that breaks.

## Impact

Every fork PR that touches `composer.lock` shows a failed check. Maintainers learn to
ignore a red X, and outside contributors see their PR marked as failing for a reason
they cannot fix and that has nothing to do with their change. The job never gates
anything, so the failure carries no information.

## Fix

Skip the comment step when the token cannot write, and say why:

```yaml
      - uses: marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment@5770ad5eb8f42dd2c4f34da00c94c5381e49af88 # v3.0.5
        # A fork PR gets a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN whatever `permissions:` asks for,
        # so posting the comment would 403. Skip rather than fail the check.
        if: >-
          ${{ steps.composer_diff.outputs.composer_diff_exit_code != 0
              && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
```

Do **not** switch the trigger to `pull_request_target` to get a writable token: that
runs with the base repository's secrets against a fork's `composer.lock`, and
`IonBazan/composer-diff-action` reads that attacker-controlled file. The skip is the
correct trade — internal PRs keep the comment, fork PRs lose a convenience.

## Resolution
Comment step now also requires head.repo.full_name == github.repository, so fork PRs skip instead of 403ing. pull_request_target explicitly ruled out in a comment.
title: composer-diff workflow fails on every fork pull request

## Problem

The lint and the fix-lint scripts are two unrelated tools:

```json
"lint":     "vendor/bin/phpcs",
"lint-fix": "vendor/bin/php-cs-fixer fix --rules @PSR2 ."
```

`composer lint` is `phpcs`, driven by `phpcs.xml` — which scopes the run to
`src bin tools test`, excludes `vendor`, and excludes `test/Acme/*` with a comment
explaining that those fixtures are deliberate, permanent PSR-2 violations.

`composer lint-fix` is `friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer`. There is no `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php` in
the repository, so it honours none of that: no path scoping, no exclusions, and its own
interpretation of `@PSR2`.

Running the documented "fix" for the documented "lint" therefore rewrites files the lint
accepts, and rewrites the fixtures the lint is configured to leave alone.

## Evidence

`phpcs` is clean, and so is its own fixer:

```
$ vendor/bin/phpcs
....................... 23 / 23 (100%)
$ vendor/bin/phpcbf
No violations were found
```

`php-cs-fixer` with the same nominal standard disagrees about six files:

```
$ vendor/bin/php-cs-fixer fix --rules @PSR2 --dry-run --using-cache=no .
   1) test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php
   2) test/UtilsTest.php
   3) test/Acme/Fixtures/Types/Aliasing.php
   4) test/ReflectorTest.php
   5) src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php
   6) src/PHPDocsMD/Reflections/Reflector.php

Fixed 6 of 46 files
```

Two are `src/` files that `composer lint` and CI both pass. One is
`test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php` — the fixture `phpcs.xml` excludes by name, with
a comment saying it "must keep its CRLF endings" because a test depends on them.
`composer lint-fix` normalises it.

The dependency is otherwise unused: `php-cs-fixer` appears in no workflow, no other script,
and no config file, and it is the heaviest entry in `require-dev` — it pulls in
`clue/ndjson-react`, `react/child-process`, `react/event-loop`, `react/stream`,
`evenement/evenement`, `composer/xdebug-handler`, `fidry/cpu-core-counter`,
`ergebnis/agent-detector` and the `symfony/{finder,filesystem,process,stopwatch,options-resolver,event-dispatcher}`
set, none of which any other tool here needs.

## Impact

The one command a contributor is told to run to fix lint output silently reformats source
that already passes and destroys a test fixture, and nothing in CI catches it because CI
runs `composer lint`, never `composer lint-fix`. The two commands cannot both be right, and
the repository ships no configuration that would reconcile them.

## Fix

`php_codesniffer` already ships the fixer for the ruleset in use. Point the script at it
and delete the redundant dependency:

```json
"lint":     "vendor/bin/phpcs",
"lint-fix": "vendor/bin/phpcbf",
```

```
composer remove --dev friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer
```

`phpcbf` reads the same `phpcs.xml`, so the exclusions and the file list are the ones the
lint already enforces, and `composer lint-fix && composer lint` becomes a fixed point.

If a second formatter is genuinely wanted later, it needs a `.php-cs-fixer.dist.php` that
reproduces `phpcs.xml`'s exclusions — including `test/Acme/` — before it may be wired to a
script.

## Resolution
lint-fix is now vendor/bin/phpcbf, driven by the same phpcs.xml as composer lint; friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer removed along with 10 transitive packages. Verified: lint-fix now changes nothing (md5 of every PHP file identical before/after) and leaves the CRLF fixture intact.
title: composer lint-fix runs a different tool with different rules than composer lint

## Problem

`PHPDocsMDCommand::buildTableGenerator()` falls back to the default generator whenever the
slug is neither a loadable class nor a known key:

```php
$map = [
    'default' => MDTableGenerator::class,
];

$class = $map[$tableGeneratorSlug] ?? $map['default'];

return new $class();
```

A misspelled class name, a class that is not autoloadable from the current working
directory, or a slug that does not exist all take the `?? $map['default']` arm. The run
succeeds, the document is produced in the wrong format, and the exit status is 0.

## Evidence

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --tableGenerator=NoSuchGeneratorClass src | head -3
## Table of contents

- [\PHPDocsMD\DocInfo](#class-phpdocsmd-docinfo)
$ echo $?
0
```

The same command with a *valid* class name that does not implement the interface is
rejected loudly, and the neighbouring option rejects unknown values too:

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --visibility=private src
In Reflector.php line 144:
  Unknown visibility "private". Supported: public, protected, abstract, final
$ echo $?
1
```

So the fail-open path is not a deliberate policy — it is the one option that does not
validate. README.md:96 documents the option as taking a "Slug or fully-qualified class
name of a `PHPDocsMD\TableGenerator` implementation", which states no fallback.

## Impact

A build that asks for a custom table format and gets the built-in one instead reports
success. In CI the failure surfaces as a docs diff that looks like an unrelated formatting
regression, or — where the docs are regenerated and committed automatically — not at all.
The user's most likely mistake with this option, a typo or an unregistered autoload path,
is precisely the one the code refuses to report.

## Fix

Reject anything that is neither a known slug nor a usable class:

```php
$map = [
    'default' => MDTableGenerator::class,
];

if (!isset($map[$tableGeneratorSlug])) {
    throw new InvalidArgumentException(
        sprintf(
            'Unknown table generator "%s". Use a supported slug (%s) or the fully qualified '
            . 'name of a class implementing %s.',
            $tableGeneratorSlug,
            implode(', ', array_keys($map)),
            TableGenerator::class
        )
    );
}

return new $map[$tableGeneratorSlug]();
```

The `class_exists()` branch above is unchanged, so a real custom generator still works and
one that does not implement the interface still gets its existing message.

Add to `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` a case asserting `InvalidArgumentException` for
`--tableGenerator=NoSuchGeneratorClass`, mirroring the existing unknown-visibility test.

## Resolution
buildTableGenerator() throws InvalidArgumentException on a slug that is neither a known key nor a loadable class. Test: testAnUnknownTableGeneratorIsRejected.
title: An unknown --tableGenerator value silently produces default output and exits 0

## Problem

`DocInfoExtractor::getCleanDocComment()` strips the docblock's `*` decoration with an
unanchored pattern:

```php
return trim(trim((string)preg_replace('/([\s|^]\*\s)/', '', $comment)), '*');
```

`[\s|^]` is a character class — whitespace, a literal `|`, or a literal `^` — followed by
`*` followed by any whitespace. Nothing ties it to the start of a line, so it matches an
asterisk *anywhere* in the prose, and deletes it together with one character on each side.

Multiplication, glob patterns, `char *ptr`, wildcard notation and markdown emphasis in a
description are all silently mangled.

## Evidence

```php
/**
 * Area is width * height in pixels.
 */
class Star
{
    /**
     * Multiply 2 * 3 to get six.
     */
    public function calc(): int { return 6; }
}
```

```
$ php probe.php
class desc: 'Area is widthheight in pixels.'
fn calc desc: 'Multiply 23 to get six.'
```

`width * height` became `widthheight`; `2 * 3` became `23`. Neither the space before nor
the space after survives, so the two words are joined and the sentence changes meaning
without any visible marker that text was removed.

## Impact

The single job of this tool is to reproduce docblock prose in markdown. It silently
deletes characters from that prose. The corruption is invisible in review — the sentence
still reads as a sentence — and there is no warning, no diff, and no way for the author to
tell from the output that the source said something else.

## Fix

The decoration only ever appears at the start of a line, so anchor the match there and
consume exactly the same three characters it consumes today (one leading whitespace, the
`*`, one trailing whitespace):

```php
return trim(trim((string)preg_replace('/^([ \t]*)[ \t]\*(\s)/m', '$1', $comment)), '*');
```

`^...$1` re-emits the indentation minus the one space the old pattern ate, so the leading
whitespace `formatExampleComment()`'s `\n {7}` / `\n {4}` / `\n {3}` heuristics depend on
is unchanged. Keep `\s` (not `[ \t]`) as the trailing class so a blank `*` line is consumed
exactly as it is today.

Verify with `composer docs-check` — it must produce no diff — and add a
`DocInfoExtractorTest` (or a `Docblocks` fixture) asserting that a description containing
`a * b` round-trips intact.

## Resolution
The '*' strip is anchored to the start of a line and re-emits the indentation, so an asterisk in prose survives and the example indentation the formatter measures is unchanged. Test: testAnAsteriskInADescriptionSurvives.
title: An asterisk inside a docblock description is deleted along with the spaces around it

body: ## Problem `MDTableGenerator::addFunc()` opens one ``, closes it after the function name when there are parameters, and then closes it a second time after the argument list: ```php $str = ''; ... $str .= self::escapeCell($func->getName()) . '('; if ($func->hasParams()) { ... $str .= '' . implode(', ', $params) . ')'; // <- closes the opening tag } else { $str .= ')'; } $str .= ' : ' . self::escapeCell($func->getReturnType()) . ''; // <- closes it again ``` With no parameters the two branches balance: `name()`. With parameters the tag is closed after `(` and then closed again after `)`, so the row carries one `` that opens nothing. The `str_replace(['', ' '], ...)` further down cannot repair it — neither sequence ever occurs, because the parameter list always begins with `` and always ends with `)` before the second closer. ## Evidence Counted over the repository's own committed `docs.md`: ``` table rows: 102, unbalanced: 67 ``` 67 of 102 rows — every row for a function that takes at least one parameter. Three of them: ``` | public | __construct(array $data=[]) : void | | public | getParameterInfo(string $name) : array | | public | applyInfoToEntity(... $reflection, ...) : void | ``` `` appears twice, `` three times. The parameterless rows in the same table are balanced: ``` | public | getTable() : string | ``` ## Impact Two thirds of every generated document is invalid HTML, including the `docs.md` this repository publishes and links to from its README. Browsers and GitHub's sanitiser discard the stray tag, which is why it has gone unnoticed; a strict consumer does not. Pandoc, markdown-to-HTML pipelines that validate, static-site generators that parse the embedded HTML into a DOM, and anything converting the document to a non-HTML format all see a close tag with no open and either drop the row's formatting or error. ## Fix Emit the closing parenthesis and the closing tag from one place, so both branches balance: ```php $str .= self::escapeCell($func->getName()) . '('; if ($func->hasParams()) { $params = []; foreach ($func->getParams() as $param) { ... } $str .= '' . implode(', ', $params) . ''; } $str .= ') : ' . self::escapeCell($func->getReturnType()) . ''; ``` No parameters gives `name()` exactly as before. With parameters it gives `name(…)`, and the existing `'' => ''` replacement then collapses the last parameter's closer with the new opener, so the rendered result is `$name)` — balanced, and visually identical to today. This changes `docs.md`, so regenerate it with `composer docs` in the same commit. Add to `MDTableGeneratorTest` an assertion that `substr_count($row, '') === substr_count($row, '')` for a function with parameters and for one without. ## Resolution addFunc() re-opens before the closing parenthesis so the trailing closer has something to close. docs.md unbalanced rows 67 -> 0; across the 80-package corpus 11005 -> 0. Test: testEveryRowBalancesItsMarkupTags. The existing testFuncWithAllFeatures expectation encoded the unbalanced output and was corrected.
title: Every function row with parameters emits an unmatched closing strong tag

## Problem

`MDTableGenerator::formatExampleComment()` wraps the example in a three-backtick fence
without looking at what the example contains:

```php
return sprintf("```%s\n%s\n```", $type, trim($example));
```

CommonMark closes a fenced block at the first fence of at least the same length. An
`@example` written in the increasingly common markdown style — with its own ``` fence,
which is what phpDocumentor and every IDE docblock preview render — therefore closes the
wrapper on its opening line, and the wrapper's closing fence opens a *new* block.

## Evidence

```php
namespace Probe;

class Fenced
{
    /**
     * Uses a markdown fence inside the example.
     *
     * @example
     * ```
     * $x = [1, 2, 3];
     * ```
     */
    public function fenced() {}
}
```

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\Fenced'
###### Examples of Fenced::fenced()
```
```
$x = [1, 2, 3];
```
```
```

Four consecutive fence lines. Rendered, that is: an empty code block, the example body as
plain prose, another empty code block. The code is not in a code block at all.

Found in the wild in an installed dependency —
`PhpCsFixer\RuleCustomisation\RuleCustomisationPolicyInterface::getRuleCustomisers()`,
whose `@example` is a fenced array literal. There the inner closing fence is indented, so
it does not close anything, and the wrapper's closing fence opens a block that never
terminates:

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate vendor/friendsofphp/php-cs-fixer
 1410| ```
 1411| ```
 1412|     [
 1413|  'array_syntax' => static function (\SplFileInfo $file) {
 ...
 1428|     ```
 1429| ```          <- opens a block that runs to the end of the section
```

That document ends with an odd number of fences (5), which is how the defect was found —
scanning 102 generated packages for unbalanced fences returned exactly this one.

## Impact

The example — the part of a docblock most likely to contain the characters markdown cares
about — is rendered as markdown instead of as code. Array literals become lists, `_` pairs
become emphasis, and in the unterminated case everything after the example, including the
next class's heading and tables, is swallowed into a code block.

The failure is invisible in the raw output, which still contains all the text. It appears
only once rendered.

## Fix

Use a fence longer than any fence inside the content, which is exactly what CommonMark
prescribes for nesting:

```php
$type = '';

// A very naive analysis of the programming language used in the comment
if (str_contains($example, '<?php')) {
    $type = 'php';
} elseif (str_contains($example, 'var ') && !str_contains($example, '</')) {
    $type = 'js';
}

$example = trim($example);

// The fence must be longer than any fence inside the example, or the example's
// own ``` closes this one and everything after it renders as prose.
$longest = preg_match_all('/`{3,}/', $example, $matches)
    ? max(array_map('strlen', $matches[0]))
    : 0;
$fence = str_repeat('`', max(3, $longest + 1));

return sprintf("%s%s\n%s\n%s", $fence, $type, $example, $fence);
```

An example with no fences keeps the three-backtick wrapper, so `docs.md` and every existing
test are unaffected — verify that with `composer docs-check` (no diff) and
`vendor/bin/phpunit`.

Add to `MDTableGeneratorTest` a case whose example contains a ``` fence, asserting the
rendered block opens and closes with four backticks and that the total fence count is even.

## Resolution
formatExampleComment() sizes the fence at one backtick longer than the longest fence inside the example. Corpus files with an unclosed fence 1 -> 0. Test: testAnExampleContainingAFenceGetsALongerFence.
title: An @example containing a markdown fence breaks out of the code block it is wrapped in

## Problem `MDTableGenerator::escapeCell()` neutralises the one character that ends a markdown *cell* and nothing that ends a *row*: ```php private static function escapeCell(string $str): string { return str_replace('|', '\\|', $str); } ``` A markdown table row must occupy exactly one line. Parameter defaults come straight from `ReflectionParameter::getDefaultValue()` and are rendered verbatim by `Reflector::createParameterEntity()`: ```php if (is_string($def)) { $def = "`'$def'`"; } ``` so a default string containing `\n` or `\r` is emitted into the middle of a row. ## Evidence Minimal reproduction: ```php namespace Probe; /** A class whose default value spans lines. */ class Multi { public function __construct(string $header = "--- Original\n+++ New\n") {} public function after(): string { return ''; } } ``` ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\Multi' | Visibility | Function | |:-----------|:---------| | public | __construct(string $header=`'--- Original +++ New '`) : void | | public | after() : string | ``` The row occupies three lines. A markdown parser stops the table at the first line that is not a row, so the table ends after `| public | __construct(...`, and everything after it — including the intact `after()` row — renders as loose paragraph text. The class's function table is gone, not merely misformatted. This is not a synthetic case. Generating documentation for the installed dependency tree produced 13 such rows, one of them in `sebastian/diff`: ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate vendor/sebastian/diff | public | __construct(string $header=`'--- Original +++ New '`) : void | ``` `SebastianBergmann\Diff\Diff::__construct()` declares `string $header = "--- Original\n+++ New\n"` — an ordinary default for a diff header. ## Impact One multi-line default anywhere in a class silently deletes that class's entire function table from the rendered document. The generator exits 0, the raw markdown still contains the text, and nothing in the output signals that a table was truncated — the damage is visible only after rendering. ## Fix Escape the row terminator alongside the cell terminator, in the one place every cell already passes through: ```php /** * An unescaped pipe terminates the cell it sits in, so a union type such as * "int | string" would silently add a column to the row. A newline terminates * the whole row, so a multi-line default value would truncate the table — both * have to be neutralised here, where every cell passes through. */ private static function escapeCell(string $str): string { return str_replace( ['|', "\r\n", "\r", "\n"], ['\\|', '
', '
', '
'], $str ); } ``` `
` is already used inside these cells for descriptions and deprecation notices, so the multi-line default renders as multiple lines within its cell instead of breaking out of it. Order matters: `\r\n` must be replaced before the bare `\r`. Add to `MDTableGeneratorTest` a case with a parameter defaulting to a string containing `\n`, asserting the produced row contains no newline. ## Resolution escapeCell() converts CRLF/CR/LF to
alongside the pipe escape. Corpus rows split across lines 30 -> 0. Test: testANewlineInADefaultValueCannotBreakTheRow.
title: A newline in a default value breaks out of the table row and destroys the table

body: ## Problem `Reflector::createParameterEntity()` builds the displayed parameter name from the bare reflection name and nothing else: ```php $varName = '$' . $reflection->getName(); ... $param->setName($docs['name'] ?? $varName); ``` `ReflectionParameter::getName()` returns `rest` for `string ...$rest` and `out` for `array &$out` — the `...` and the `&` are separate flags (`isVariadic()`, `isPassedByReference()`) that are never read. The docblock cannot supply them either. `DocInfoExtractor::figureOutParamDeclaration()` keys the parsed entry by the name as written: ```php $name = current(explode('=', $name)); ... return [$name, $data]; ``` so `@param string ...$rest` is stored under `...$rest`, while `Reflector::getParams()` looks it up as `'$' . $param->getName()`: ```php $paramName = '$' . $param->getName(); $params[$param->getName()] = $this->createParameterEntity($param, $docInfo->getParameterInfo($paramName)); ``` `$rest` never matches `...$rest`, so the docblock entry is discarded and `$varName` — the marker-less form — is used. ## Evidence ```php namespace Probe; class Mods { /** * @param string $first the ordinary one * @param string ...$rest the variadic one */ public function variadic(string $first, string ...$rest) {} /** @param array &$out filled by the callee */ public function byRef(array &$out) {} } ``` ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\Mods' | public | byRef(array $out) : void | | public | variadic(string $first, string $rest) : void | ``` Neither marker survives. Across documentation generated for symfony/console, phpunit/phpunit, nikic/php-parser and webmozart/assert — which between them declare 74 variadic methods — the rendered output contains zero `...` markers: ``` $ grep -rhoE '\.\.\.' out/*.md | wc -l 0 ``` ## Impact The rendered signature is not the signature. `variadic(string $first, string $rest)` says the method takes exactly two arguments; it takes one or more. `byRef(array $out)` says the argument is not modified; it is the method's only output. Someone writing a call from the documentation writes the wrong call, and for the by-reference case writes one that compiles and silently discards the result. This is a generated API reference: the signature line is the part readers trust most. ## Fix Take the markers from reflection, which is authoritative, and make the docblock lookup find its entry regardless of how the author wrote the name. In `Reflector::createParameterEntity()`: ```php // isVariadic()/isPassedByReference() are separate flags; getName() returns the // bare name, so without these the rendered signature is not the signature. $prefix = $reflection->isVariadic() ? '...$' : ($reflection->isPassedByReference() ? '&$' : '$'); $varName = $prefix . $reflection->getName(); ... $param->setName($varName); ``` Using `$varName` unconditionally — rather than `$docs['name'] ?? $varName` — is what keeps the two consistent when the docblock omits a marker the signature has, or carries one it does not. In `DocInfoExtractor::figureOutParamDeclaration()`, key by the normalised name so the entry is findable: ```php $name = current(explode('=', $name)); // Key by the bare name: Reflector looks parameters up as "$name", and a // docblock may write "...$name" or "&$name" for the same parameter. $key = '$' . ltrim($name, '&.$'); $data = [ 'description' => $description, 'name' => $name, 'type' => $type, 'default' => false, ]; return [$key, $data]; ``` The documented *type* and *description* are then applied to variadic and by-reference parameters too, which they currently are not. Add to `ReflectorTest` a fixture with a variadic and a by-reference parameter, asserting the rendered names are `...$rest` and `&$out` and that the documented type reaches both. Verify `composer docs-check`: `Reflector::mergeTypeDeclarations`-style variadic helpers and `UseInspector` take no variadics today, so `docs.md` should be unchanged — confirm rather than assume. ## Resolution The rendered name carries '...' or '&' from ReflectionParameter, and figureOutParamDeclaration() keys entries by the bare name so a docblock written '...$rest' or '&$out' reaches its parameter. Test: testVariadicAndByReferenceMarkersAreRendered.
title: Variadic and by-reference parameters render as ordinary parameters

body: ## Problem `Reflector::getReturnType()` decides whether the declared return type may override the docblock by comparing the docblock type against the entity's *default*: ```php if ($func->getReturnType() !== $returnType && $method->hasReturnType()) { $returnType = $this->getReturnTypeFromMethod($method, $returnType); } ``` At that point `$func` has just been constructed and `applyInfoToEntity()` has set only name, description, example, see, internal and deprecated — never the return type. So `$func->getReturnType()` is always `FunctionEntity`'s initialiser, the literal string `'void'` (FunctionEntity.php:18). The guard therefore reduces to `'void' !== $returnType`: the declared return type is consulted for every docblock *except* one that says `@return void`, which is the one case where it is silently discarded. ## Evidence ```php namespace Probe; class Ret { /** @return void */ public function typed(): string { return 'x'; } /** @return int */ public function typed2(): string { return 'x'; } } ``` ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\Ret' | public | typed() : void | | public | typed2() : string | ``` `typed()` returns a `string` — the signature says so and PHP enforces it — but the document states `void`. `typed2()`, whose docblock is wrong in exactly the same way, is corrected to `string`, which is the behaviour the tool intends everywhere else: the declared type wins because it is the one the engine enforces. ## Impact A stale `@return void` left behind when a method gained a real return type is published as fact, and it is published as the *opposite* of the truth — a reader is told the method returns nothing. Every other contradictory docblock is corrected, so the output gives no hint that this one was trusted. ## Fix Drop the comparison against the default. The declared type is authoritative, and `getReturnTypeFromMethod()` already falls back to the docblock when the declaration is empty: ```php if ($method->hasReturnType()) { $returnType = $this->getReturnTypeFromMethod($method, $returnType); } ``` This changes behaviour for exactly one input class — a docblock whose `@return` is `void` — because the removed condition was true for every other value. Add to `ReflectorTest` (or a `Docblocks` fixture): a method declared `: string` with `@return void`, asserting the documented type is `string`. Verify `composer docs-check` produces no diff. ## Resolution Removed the comparison against FunctionEntity's 'void' initialiser; the declared return type now always wins, which changes behaviour only for '@return void'. Test: testADocblockSayingVoidDoesNotSuppressTheDeclaredType.
title: A docblock saying @return void suppresses the method's declared return type
