## Problem

`PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testClassInACrlfFileIsDiscovered()` exists to prove that
"[w]hether a class is found must not depend on the line endings of the file it is
declared in". It reads one fixture:

```php
public function testClassInACrlfFileIsDiscovered(): void
{
    $this->tester->execute(['class' => __DIR__ . '/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds']);
    $this->assertStringContainsString('Acme\\Fixtures\\Kinds\\CrLfClass', $this->tester->getDisplay());
}
```

`test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php` has LF line endings. There is not one carriage
return in it. The fixture is byte-for-byte the same *kind* of file as `PlainClass.php`
sitting beside it, which the previous test already covers, so the assertion is satisfied
by the plain-file code path and the CRLF path is never entered.

## Evidence

```
$ for f in test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/*.php; do
    printf "%-45s CR=%s LF=%s\n" "$f" "$(tr -cd '\r' < $f | wc -c)" "$(tr -cd '\n' < $f | wc -c)"
  done
test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php        CR=0 LF=13
test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/PlainClass.php       CR=0 LF=13
test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/PlainEnum.php        CR=0 LF=17
test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/PlainTrait.php       CR=0 LF=14

$ file test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php
test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php: PHP script, ASCII text
```

`cat -A` confirms every line ends `$`, never `^M$`. The fixture's own docblock states
"Declared in a file with CRLF line endings." — it is not.

Two configuration files carry comments asserting the opposite, and both are now describing
a property the file does not have:

```
# .gitattributes
/test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php     -text

<!-- phpcs.xml -->
CrLfClass.php must keep its CRLF endings. Both are permanent PSR-2 violations
that cannot be fixed without changing what is under test.
```

`-text` tells git to store the bytes verbatim; with LF bytes committed it preserves LF, so
the attribute does not restore what was never there.

## Impact

A regression test that reports green while covering nothing is worse than no test: the
codebase carries three separate written claims that line-ending handling is guarded, and a
future change to `findClassInFile()`'s tokenising — the thing the test exists to protect —
would ship undetected past a full green suite.

## Fix

Give the fixture the endings it claims, and make the test fail loudly if they are ever
normalised away:

```php
public function testClassInACrlfFileIsDiscovered(): void
{
    $fixture = __DIR__ . '/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/CrLfClass.php';
    self::assertStringContainsString(
        "\r\n",
        (string)file_get_contents($fixture),
        'the CRLF fixture has been normalised to LF — this test would pass vacuously'
    );

    $this->tester->execute(['class' => __DIR__ . '/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds']);

    $this->assertStringContainsString('Acme\\Fixtures\\Kinds\\CrLfClass', $this->tester->getDisplay());
}
```

Rewrite the fixture with CRLF (`printf` or `unix2dos`) and confirm with
`tr -cd '\r' < … | wc -c` before committing. The guard assertion is what keeps the
`.gitattributes` `-text` rule and the `phpcs.xml` comment honest.

## Resolution
Fixture rewritten with real CRLF (13 CR bytes, 'with CRLF line terminators'), and the test now asserts the fixture still contains \r\n before exercising the behaviour, so a future normalisation fails loudly instead of passing vacuously. Verified it survives composer lint-fix.
title: The CRLF fixture contains no CRLF, so the test guarding line-ending handling proves nothing

## Problem

Both workflows check out with `actions/checkout` at its default `persist-credentials: true`,
which writes an `http.extraheader` holding the `GITHUB_TOKEN` into `.git/config` and leaves
it there for the rest of the job.

`php.yml` then runs, in this order: `composer validate`, `composer install`/`composer
update`, `composer audit`, `phpunit`, `phpcs`, `psalm`. Everything from the install step
onward is third-party code executing in the same workspace as the persisted credential.

The workflow already states this threat model and stops one step short of the control that
addresses it:

```yaml
# Every step here only reads the repository. composer install/update run
# third-party code, so the token they see must not be able to write anything.
permissions:
  contents: read
```

`permissions:` bounds what the token *can do*; it does not stop the token from being read
out of `.git/config`, uploaded with an artifact, or picked up by a `.git`-copying step.

`composer-diff.yml` is the sharper case: its token carries `pull-requests: write`, and the
step that runs immediately after checkout is a third-party action
(`IonBazan/composer-diff-action`) operating on a pull request's `composer.lock`.

## Evidence

```
$ zizmor .github/workflows
help[artipacked]: credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts
  --> .github/workflows/composer-diff.yml:14:9
   | does not set persist-credentials: false
help[artipacked]: credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts
  --> .github/workflows/php.yml:57:9
   | does not set persist-credentials: false

error[excessive-permissions]: overly broad permissions
 --> .github/workflows/composer-diff.yml:7:3
  |
7 |   pull-requests: write
  |   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ pull-requests: write is overly broad at the workflow level

warning[excessive-permissions]: overly broad permissions
  --> .github/workflows/semantic-commits.yml:1:1
```

`semantic-commits.yml` has no workflow-level `permissions:` block at all, so its token
starts from the repository default and is narrowed only inside the single job; any job
added later inherits the default instead of nothing.

`actionlint` reports no issues, and `gitleaks` finds no committed secrets over all 182
commits — the exposure here is runtime, not committed.

## Impact

Neither workflow needs git credentials after checkout: nothing pushes, tags, or calls the
API through git. Leaving them in the workspace means any compromised package in the
dependency tree — the thing `composer audit` and `roave/security-advisories` exist to
guard against — gets a token as well as code execution. For `composer-diff.yml` that token
can comment on and modify pull requests.

## Fix

Turn persistence off at every checkout:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Nothing here uses git credentials after checkout; not persisting them
          # keeps the token out of .git/config while composer runs third-party code.
          persist-credentials: false
```

and in `composer-diff.yml`, which also needs `fetch-depth: 0`:

```yaml
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Required to make it possible to compare with PR base branch
          persist-credentials: false
```

Move that workflow's grant down to the job that needs it, so a second job cannot inherit
PR-write:

```yaml
permissions: {}

jobs:
  composer-diff:
    permissions:
      # The sticky-comment step posts the diff back onto the pull request.
      pull-requests: write
```

Add the same `permissions: {}` default to `semantic-commits.yml`, which already narrows
correctly at job level.

Verify with `zizmor .github/workflows` — the two `artipacked` findings and both
`excessive-permissions` findings must disappear — and confirm the `php.yml` matrix still
checks out and installs.

## Resolution
persist-credentials: false on both checkouts; composer-diff.yml and semantic-commits.yml default to permissions: {} with the write grant moved to the job that needs it. zizmor now reports no findings (was 2 low + 2 excessive-permissions); actionlint clean.
title: Checkout leaves the GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config before third-party code runs

## Problem

`PHPDocsMDCommand::isDocumentable()` reports a class it could not load by writing to the
process's STDERR handle rather than through the command's `OutputInterface`:

```php
} catch (\Throwable $e) {
    fwrite(
        STDERR,
        sprintf('phpdoc-md: skipping %s (%s)%s', $className, $e->getMessage(), PHP_EOL)
    );

    return false;
}
```

Symfony's console gives a command two things this bypasses: verbosity control, and a
capturable output stream. Neither applies to a raw `fwrite`.

## Evidence

`--quiet` does not silence it:

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate -q test/Acme/Fixtures/Broken
phpdoc-md: skipping \Acme\Fixtures\Broken\UnloadableChild (Class "Acme\Fixtures\Broken\NotInstalled\MissingBase" not found)
```

`CommandTester` cannot see it, so it lands in the test runner's own output instead —
visible in every run of the suite, in the middle of the progress bar:

```
$ vendor/bin/phpunit
..................................phpdoc-md: skipping \Acme\Fixtures\Broken\UnloadableChild (Class "Acme\Fixtures\Broken\NotInstalled\MissingBase" not found)
............................... 65 / 94 ( 69%)
```

`PHPDocsMDCommandTest`'s unloadable-class test therefore asserts only that the other
classes still appear and the exit code is 0; the message itself — the part that tells a
user why a class is missing from their documentation — is not asserted anywhere, because
the test has no way to read it.

## Impact

The one diagnostic this tool emits cannot be suppressed, cannot be redirected by Symfony's
own mechanisms, and cannot be tested. It corrupts the PHPUnit progress line on every run,
which trains readers to ignore output from a passing suite.

## Fix

Capture the error stream in `execute()` and write through it:

```php
private ?OutputInterface $errorOutput = null;

protected function execute(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
{
    $this->errorOutput = $output instanceof ConsoleOutputInterface
        ? $output->getErrorOutput()
        : $output;
    ...
}
```

```php
} catch (\Throwable $e) {
    $this->errorOutput?->writeln(
        sprintf('phpdoc-md: skipping %s (%s)', $className, $e->getMessage()),
        OutputInterface::OUTPUT_RAW
    );

    return false;
}
```

`OUTPUT_RAW` matters for the same reason it does on the document writes at lines 296-314:
an exception message may contain angle brackets that Symfony's formatter would otherwise
consume. `writeln()` honours `--quiet`, and `ConsoleOutput`'s error stream still goes to
STDERR so `generate src > api.md` keeps working unchanged.

Then extend the existing unloadable-class test in `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` to assert the
message, constructing the tester with `['capture_stderr_separately' => true]`.

## Resolution
The diagnostic goes through ConsoleOutputInterface::getErrorOutput() with OUTPUT_RAW, so it honours --quiet and CommandTester can read it. The PHPUnit progress bar is no longer polluted. Test: testTheSkippedClassWarningGoesThroughTheConsoleOutput.
title: The skipped-class warning writes to STDERR directly, bypassing the console output

## Problem

`OPT_TABLE_GENERATOR` is declared `InputOption::VALUE_OPTIONAL`. Symfony returns `null`,
not the declared default, when such an option is present with no value and no following
token to consume. The value is passed straight into a `string`-typed parameter:

```php
$tableGeneratorSlug = $input->getOption(self::OPT_TABLE_GENERATOR);
$tableGenerator = $this->buildTableGenerator($tableGeneratorSlug);
```

```php
protected function buildTableGenerator(string $tableGeneratorSlug = 'default'): TableGenerator
```

The other two optional options are guarded — `--visibility` goes through `empty()`
(line 125) and `--methodRegex` through a `(string)` cast (line 131). This one is not.

## Evidence

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate src --tableGenerator
phpdoc-md: PHPDocsMD\Console\PHPDocsMDCommand::buildTableGenerator(): Argument #1
($tableGeneratorSlug) must be of type string, null given, called in
/home/ivuorinen/Code/ivuorinen/markdowndocs/src/PHPDocsMD/Console/PHPDocsMDCommand.php on line 158
$ echo $?
2
```

The same option earlier in the command line does not reproduce it, because Symfony then
consumes the next token as the value:

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --tableGenerator src
  Not enough arguments (missing: "class").
```

which is its own trap — `src` was silently eaten as the generator name.

## Impact

A user who writes the flag without a value gets an internal method signature, an absolute
path from the maintainer's machine, and exit code 2 instead of a usage error. It is a
cosmetic failure, but it is the kind that sends people to the issue tracker.

## Fix

Default the value at the call site, matching how the sibling options are handled:

```php
$tableGeneratorSlug = $input->getOption(self::OPT_TABLE_GENERATOR) ?? 'default';
```

`--tableGenerator` with no value then means "the default generator", which is the same
thing `--visibility` with no value already means for its own filter.

Add to `PHPDocsMDCommandTest` a case running the command with the option set to `null`,
asserting exit code 0 and default-generator output.

## Resolution
getOption(OPT_TABLE_GENERATOR) ?? 'default' at the call site, matching how the sibling optional options are guarded. Test: testTableGeneratorWithoutAValueFallsBackToTheDefault.
title: --tableGenerator with no value crashes with a raw TypeError

body: ## Problem The cross-reference substitution in `PHPDocsMDCommand::execute()` only matches a class name that sits immediately after `` or `/`: ```php $docString = preg_replace( '/(|\/)' . preg_quote($className, '/') . '(?![\w\\\\])/', ... ); ``` Inside a union, only the first member has `` in front of it. `MDTableGenerator::escapeCell()` renders the separator as `\|`, so every later member is preceded by `\| ` — which the alternation does not accept. Those members are never linked, even when the class is documented in the same file and already present in `$classLinks`. ## Evidence `test/Acme/Fixtures/Links` declares `Bar`, `BarBaz` and a method returning both. Generated output: ``` makeEither(...) : [\Acme\Fixtures\Links\Bar](#interface-acme-fixtures-links-bar) \| \Acme\Fixtures\Links\BarBaz ``` `\Acme\Fixtures\Links\Bar` — first member, directly after `` — is linked. `\Acme\Fixtures\Links\BarBaz` — second member — is plain text. The single-type case for the same class proves the link exists and would be correct: ``` makeBarBaz() : [\Acme\Fixtures\Links\BarBaz](#class-acme-fixtures-links-barbaz) ``` ## Impact Every union-typed return value and parameter loses navigation for all members after the first. Union types are ordinary in modern PHP, and the failure is invisible in review: the type renders correctly, it just is not a link. The more precisely a project types its API, the more links it loses. ## Fix Accept the escaped pipe as a leading context alongside `` and `/`: ```php $docString = preg_replace( '/(|\\\\\| |\/)' . preg_quote($className, '/') . '(?![\w\\\\])/', '$1' . str_replace(['\\', '$'], ['\\\\', '\\$'], $link), $docString ); ``` The capture group is already re-emitted as `$1`, so the separator survives. Verify against the shape the escaping actually produces before committing — the number of backslashes in a single-quoted PHP string reaching a regex reaching a replacement is exactly where this class of fix goes wrong. Assert on the rendered output, not on the pattern. Add to `PHPDocsMDCommandTest`: a case asserting that both members of `makeEither`'s union return type are rendered as links. ## Note Found while re-running the suite during the fix pass for this audit's other findings; it is not one of the twelve originally filed and has not been fixed. ## Resolution The substitution accepts the escaped pipe as a leading context alongside and /, built with preg_quote rather than hand-counted backslashes. Test: testEveryMemberOfAUnionReturnTypeIsLinked.
title: Union type members after the first are never linked

## Problem `DocInfoExtractor::extractInfoFromComment()` recognises a tag with a regex that makes both braces optional and independent: ```php $isTag = preg_match('/^\{?@([A-Za-z][\w-]*)\}?$/', $words[0], $tagMatch) === 1; ``` The braces exist to admit `{@inheritDoc}`, which is written as one word. But `\{?` and `\}?` do not have to agree, so the *opening* fragment of any inline tag matches on its own: `{@link` — with the closing brace on a later word — is read as a block tag named `link`. The `else` branch then makes it the current tag and consumes the rest of the line into `$tags['link']`, a key nothing ever reads. The text is gone. Inline tags are, by definition, the ones that appear inside prose. ## Evidence ```php class Edge { /** * Uses inline links. * * {@link https://example.com Example} */ public function inline() {} } ``` ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate --bootstrap=boot.php 'Probe\Edge' | public | inline() : void
Uses inline links. | ``` The `{@link …}` line is absent from the rendered description, and no warning is emitted. Mid-sentence use survives — only `$words[0]`, the first word on the line, is tested — so the loss depends on where the author wrapped the line. ## Impact Documentation text disappears silently, and which text disappears depends on line wrapping. `{@link}`, `{@see}` and `{@internal}` are all written this way, and a line that begins with one is a normal result of reflowing a paragraph. ## Fix Require the braces to agree, so only a complete inline tag is recognised: ```php // Either "@tag" or a complete "{@tag}" — matching a bare "{@tag" would let the // opening fragment of an inline {@link ...} be read as a block tag and swallow // the rest of the line. $isTag = preg_match('/^(?:@|\{@(?=[^}]*\}$))([A-Za-z][\w-]*)\}?$/', $words[0], $tagMatch) === 1; ``` or, more plainly, two alternatives: ```php $isTag = preg_match('/^(?:\{@([A-Za-z][\w-]*)\}|@([A-Za-z][\w-]*))$/', $words[0], $tagMatch) === 1; $tagName = $isTag ? ($tagMatch[1] !== '' ? $tagMatch[1] : $tagMatch[2]) : ''; ``` `{@inheritDoc}` still matches — it is a complete braced word — which `test/Acme/Fixtures/Docblocks/BracedInheritor.php` already covers, so that fixture is the regression guard for not breaking the case the braces were added for. Add to the same fixture a method whose description contains a line beginning with `{@link https://example.com Example}`, asserting the line survives in the rendered description. ## Resolution The tag regex now requires the inline braces to agree, so '{@link' is no longer read as a block tag named 'link'. {@inheritDoc} still matches, guarded by the existing BracedInheritor fixture. Asserted in testAWrappedParamLineStaysWithItsParameter.
title: A line starting with an inline {@link} tag is swallowed and dropped from the description

## Problem

`ClassEntity::generateTitle()` knows two kinds of type:

```php
$translate = [
    '%label%' => $this->isInterface() ? 'Interface' : 'Class',
    ...
];
```

and `ClassEntityFactory::create()` only ever populates two flags:

```php
$class->isInterface($reflection->isInterface());
$class->isAbstract($reflection->isAbstract());
```

`ReflectionClass::isTrait()` and `ReflectionClass::isEnum()` are never read, so everything
that is not an interface is labelled `Class`. The title feeds `generateAnchor()` and the
table-of-contents entry as well as the heading, so the wrong word appears three times per
type.

The tool goes out of its way to *find* traits and enums —
`PHPDocsMDCommand::findClassInFile()` matches `T_TRAIT` and `T_ENUM` alongside `T_CLASS`,
`isDocumentable()` calls `trait_exists()`, README lists "class, interface, trait or enum"
as supported input, and `test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/` carries a fixture for each — and then
describes them all as classes.

## Evidence

```
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds
- [\Acme\Fixtures\Kinds\PlainEnum](#class-acme-fixtures-kinds-plainenum)
- [\Acme\Fixtures\Kinds\PlainTrait](#class-acme-fixtures-kinds-plaintrait)
### Class: \Acme\Fixtures\Kinds\PlainEnum
### Class: \Acme\Fixtures\Kinds\PlainTrait
```

```
$ php -r '... new ReflectionClass($c) ...'
Acme\Fixtures\Kinds\PlainTrait         isTrait=1 isEnum=0 isInterface=0
Acme\Fixtures\Kinds\PlainEnum          isTrait=0 isEnum=1 isInterface=0
```

Reflection reports the kind correctly; the entity never asks. 58 files in the installed
dependency tree declare a trait or an enum, so this is not a fixture-only shape.

`PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testEachKindOfTypeIsDiscovered()` asserts only that the names appear
in the output, so the suite passes with every kind mislabelled.

## Impact

A trait cannot be instantiated and an enum has closed instances; calling either a "class" in
a generated API reference tells a reader the wrong thing about how to use it. The anchor
(`#class-…-plaintrait`) and the table of contents repeat the error, so it is also what
cross-references from other pages will link to.

## Fix

Carry the kind on the entity and use it for the label. In `ClassEntity`:

```php
private bool $isTrait = false;
private bool $isEnum = false;

public function isTrait(?bool $toggle = null): bool
{
    return $toggle === null ? $this->isTrait : ($this->isTrait = $toggle);
}

public function isEnum(?bool $toggle = null): bool
{
    return $toggle === null ? $this->isEnum : ($this->isEnum = $toggle);
}
```

```php
'%label%' => match (true) {
    $this->isInterface() => 'Interface',
    $this->isTrait()     => 'Trait',
    $this->isEnum()      => 'Enum',
    default              => 'Class',
},
```

In `ClassEntityFactory::create()`:

```php
$class->isInterface($reflection->isInterface());
$class->isTrait($reflection->isTrait());
$class->isEnum($reflection->isEnum());
$class->isAbstract($reflection->isAbstract());
```

The `(abstract)` suffix logic needs no change: `isAbstract()` is false for traits and enums.

This changes anchors for traits and enums (`#class-…` becomes `#trait-…` / `#enum-…`),
which is correct but is a change to generated output — `docs.md` contains no traits or
enums, so `composer docs-check` should stay clean; confirm rather than assume.

Extend `PHPDocsMDCommandTest::testEachKindOfTypeIsDiscovered()` to assert the heading word
for each of the four fixtures in `test/Acme/Fixtures/Kinds/`, which is what turns that test
from a name check into a kind check.

## Resolution
ClassEntity carries isTrait()/isEnum(), ClassEntityFactory populates them from reflection, and generateTitle() picks the label with a match. Headings and anchors are now Trait:/#trait- and Enum:/#enum-. Test: testEachDeclarationKindIsLabelledAsItself.
title: Traits and enums are labelled Class in every heading, anchor and TOC entry

## Problem

`Reflector::createParameterEntity()` guarantees a `type` key on `$docs` at the top of the
method, then branches on whether `$docs` is empty forty lines later:

```php
if (!isset($docs['type'])) {
    $docs['type'] = '';          // line 330-332 — $docs now always has at least one key
}
...
if (empty($docs)) {              // line 366 — never true
    $docs = [
        'description' => '',
        'name' => $varName,
        'default' => $def,
        'type' => $type,
    ];
} else {
    ...
}
```

An array holding one key is not empty, whatever the value, so the first arm cannot run.
The `else` arm is the only reachable path.

This is the same class of defect as the two unreachable ternaries already resolved in this
method (audit-b3baeac0); that fix rewrote the block above line 345 and left this one.

## Evidence

Static: `$docs['type']` is assigned unconditionally at line 331 and never unset, so
`count($docs) >= 1` holds at line 366.

Runtime, by instrumenting the arm and exercising every path the project has:

```
$ # fwrite(STDERR, "REACHED-EMPTY-DOCS-ARM") injected as the first statement of the arm
$ vendor/bin/phpunit                                 # 94 tests, 270 assertions
0
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate src                       # the project's own source
0
$ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate vendor/symfony/console    # a large third-party tree
0
```

Zero hits across all three. Psalm agrees at info level:

```
Reflector.php:366 - TypeDoesNotContainType: Type array{type: mixed|string, ...} for $docs is never falsy
```

The default-value inference the dead arm would have supplied is not lost — the reachable
arm already covers it at line 391:

```php
} elseif ($type && empty($docs['type'])) {
    $docs['type'] = $type;
}
```

## Impact

Maintenance only. A reader has to prove the unreachability before they can reason about
the parameter-merging rules, and the dead arm reads as the "undocumented parameter" case,
which is misleading: undocumented parameters take the `else` arm like everything else.

## Fix

Delete the dead arm and unwrap the `else`:

```php
$docs['default'] = $def;
if ($type === 'mixed' && $def === 'null' && str_starts_with($docs['type'], '\\')) {
    $type = false;
}

if ($type && $def && ... ) {
    ...
} elseif ($type && empty($docs['type'])) {
    $docs['type'] = $type;
}
```

`$varName` is still needed below (`$param->setName($docs['name'] ?? $varName)`), so keep
its assignment. Verify with `vendor/bin/phpunit` and `composer docs-check`; both must be
unchanged, which is what proves the removal was behaviour-preserving.

## Resolution
The unreachable empty($docs) arm removed and the else unwrapped. Suite and docs-check unchanged, which is what proves the removal was behaviour-preserving.
title: The empty($docs) branch in createParameterEntity is unreachable

## Problem

`Reflector` carries a private helper that computes exactly what a public utility in the
same namespace already computes:

```php
// Reflector.php:296-305
private function stripAwayNamespace(string $className): string
{
    $lastSeparator = strrpos($className, '\\');

    return $lastSeparator === false
        ? trim($className, '\\')
        : trim(substr($className, $lastSeparator), '\\');
}
```

```php
// Utils.php:52-57
public static function getClassBaseName(string $fullClassName): string
{
    $parts = explode('\\', trim($fullClassName));

    return end($parts);
}
```

`Reflector` already uses `Utils::getClassBaseName()` — twice, in `createParameterEntity()`
at line 339 — so the class imports the utility, calls it for this exact purpose elsewhere,
and then hand-rolls it again for its one remaining caller,
`getReturnTypesArray()` at line 554.

## Evidence

The two agree on every shape that reaches them:

| input | `stripAwayNamespace` | `Utils::getClassBaseName` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `\A\B` | `strrpos` = 2, `substr` = `\B`, trim → `B` | `['', 'A', 'B']` → `B` |
| `\B` | `strrpos` = 0, `substr` = `\B`, trim → `B` | `['', 'B']` → `B` |
| `B` | `strrpos` = false → trim → `B` | `['B']` → `B` |
| `A\B` | `strrpos` = 1, `substr` = `\B`, trim → `B` | `['A', 'B']` → `B` |

`getReturnTypesArray()` has already stripped a trailing `[]` before calling, and passes a
type string, so no other shape arrives.

## Impact

Two implementations of one rule in one class, one of them needing a comment to explain a
`strrpos() === false` coercion trap that the other does not have. A future change to how
class names are split — the leading-backslash convention this codebase applies everywhere
— has to be made twice or it silently diverges.

## Fix

```php
$localName = Utils::getClassBaseName($returnType);
```

and delete `stripAwayNamespace()`. `Utils` is already imported in `Reflector`.

Verify with `vendor/bin/phpunit` and `composer docs-check`; `ReflectorTest`'s aliasing
cases (`test/Acme/Fixtures/Types/Aliasing.php`) already exercise this call path.

## Resolution
stripAwayNamespace() deleted; getReturnTypesArray() calls Utils::getClassBaseName(), which the class already used twice for the same purpose.
title: stripAwayNamespace is a private re-implementation of Utils::getClassBaseName

body: ## Problem `Utils::sanitizeDeclaration()` decides whether a type is a class reference by looking at the whole declaration. `Utils::isClassReference()` rejects only what it recognises as a native type or what contains a space, so a generic — `list`, `array`, `Collection` — passes as a single unqualified class name and gets the current namespace glued to the front of it. The `<...>` suffix also hides the base type from `getSanitizedTypeDeclaration()`, which strips a trailing `[]` but knows nothing about angle brackets — so `array` is not recognised as the native `array`. ## Evidence ``` $ php -r '... Utils::sanitizeDeclaration($t, "Psalm\Internal") ...' list -> \Psalm\Internal\list array|null -> \Psalm\Internal\array | null Collection -> \Psalm\Internal\Collection array -> array (only because of the space) ``` In generated documentation for an installed dependency: ``` $ ./bin/phpdoc-md generate vendor/vimeo/psalm | public static | negateFormula(\Psalm\Internal\list \| array $clauses) … | public static | simplifyCNF(\Psalm\Internal\list \| array $clauses) … ``` `\Psalm\Internal\list` is not a class, and `list` is not a class at all — it is psalm's generic list type. `array` escaping only because it happens to contain a space is what makes this a defect rather than a limitation: the same construct is handled two different ways depending on whether the author put a space after the comma. ## Impact Generic docblock types are ordinary in any codebase using psalm, PHPStan or modern phpDocumentor, and `array<...>` is the most common annotation of all. Each one renders a namespaced name that does not exist, and because `isClassReference()` then treats it as a class, the tool also attempts and fails to cross-reference it. ## Fix Split the parameter list off, decide on the base name, and re-attach — the same shape the code already uses for the `[]` suffix: ```php // A generic is a base type plus a parameter list. Decide on the base name // alone: the whole string used to be treated as one class name, and the // "<...>" also hid the native "array" from isNativeType(). $generic = ''; if (preg_match('/^([^<]+)(<.*>)$/', $p, $g) === 1) { $p = $g[1]; $generic = $g[2]; } if (self::shouldPrefixWithNamespace($p)) { $p = self::sanitizeClassName('\\' . trim($currentNameSpace, '\\') . '\\' . $p); } elseif (self::isClassReference($p)) { $p = self::sanitizeClassName($p); } $parts[$key] = $p . $generic; ``` The parameters inside the brackets are left as the author wrote them, which is what happens today for every generic that escaped through the space check — resolving them too is a larger change and not needed to stop the tool inventing class names. ## Note Not one of the twenty-seven findings this audit filed: found while verifying the fixes against the regenerated dependency corpus, in the three union cells that still looked wrong. Fixed in the same pass. ## Resolution A generic is split into base type plus parameter list before the class-reference decision, and the phpdoc/psalm pseudo-types (all reserved words or hyphenated, so none can be a real class) added to Utils::$nativeTypes. list, array and class-string are now left alone; Collection still resolves as a class. Test: testSanitizeDeclarationDecidesOnTheBaseTypeOfAGeneric.
title: A generic docblock type is namespace-prefixed as if it were one class name

## Problem

Class: missing-concurrency. The workflow declares no `concurrency:` group, so
every push to the same ref starts an additional run alongside the ones already
in flight.

## Evidence

zizmor 1.28.0 `-p` (pedantic persona), audit `concurrency-limits`, Low/High
confidence: "workflow is missing concurrency setting" at the `on:` key.

## Impact

Superseded runs keep consuming runner minutes and can report a stale verdict
against an outdated commit.

## Fix

Add a top-level `concurrency:` group keyed on workflow + ref with
`cancel-in-progress: true` (none of these workflows mutate external state, so
cancelling a superseded run is safe).

## Resolution
Added top-level concurrency group (workflow+ref, cancel-in-progress: true) to composer-diff.yml; zizmor -p clean.
title: composer-diff.yml has no concurrency group
